about: Requirement registry of this repository (snapshot 2026-10-11, one shared domain vocabulary) for calibrating duplicate/related thresholds where unrelated items still look alike. items: the registry; none of them duplicates another (bootstrap review, BUG-0001). duplicates: hand-written rewordings (cross_language: Spanish translations) of the item `of`. not_duplicates: [query, stored] pairs BUG-0001 reported as false duplicates.

items.title: Runs on Node.js 22.13+ using the built-in node:sqlite module
items.description: overseer shall run on Node.js 22.13 or later, storing its data through the built-in node:sqlite module without a separate SQLite driver package.
acceptance_criteria: Given package.json, when its engines field is read, then node is ">=22.13.0"
Given Node.js 22.13 or later, when overseer opens a project database, then it uses node:sqlite DatabaseSync with extension loading enabled
items.fit_criterion: package.json engines.node is ">=22.13.0"; src/core/db.ts opens databases with node:sqlite DatabaseSync; dependencies contain no SQLite driver besides the sqlite-vec extension

items.title: Serves the MCP protocol over stdio via the `overseer mcp` command
items.description: When a harness runs `overseer mcp`, overseer shall serve the Model Context Protocol over stdin and stdout until stdin closes.
acceptance_criteria: Given a harness that starts `overseer mcp`, when it sends an initialize request on stdin, then overseer answers on stdout over the MCP stdio transport.
Given a running `overseer mcp`, when stdin ends or closes, then the server closes and the process exits.

items.title: Exposes exactly twelve MCP tools
items.description: overseer shall expose exactly twelve MCP tools: find_similar, check_coverage, create_item, update_item, get_item, list_items, search, link_items, report, export_report, import_items and open_board.
acceptance_criteria: Given a connected MCP client, when it lists the tools, then the names are exactly check_coverage, create_item, export_report, find_similar, get_item, import_items, link_items, list_items, open_board, report, search, update_item.

items.title: Every MCP tool takes an optional absolute project_dir argument
items.description: overseer shall accept an optional absolute project_dir argument on every MCP tool.
acceptance_criteria: Given a connected MCP client, when it lists the tools, then every tool's input schema contains project_dir.
Given a create_item call with project_dir set to an absolute repository path, when the server cannot detect the project otherwise, then the item is created in that repository.
Given a create_item call with project_dir 'relative/path', when it runs, then the result text starts with `INVALID_INPUT: `.

items.title: Returns tool results as structuredContent plus a text rendering
items.description: When an MCP tool call succeeds, overseer shall return the result object as structuredContent together with a text content block rendering it.
acceptance_criteria: Given a successful create_item call, when the result arrives, then structuredContent is {created:true, item:{…}} and content[0].text parses as the same JSON.
Given a report call with kind coverage, when the result arrives, then content[0].text is the Markdown report starting with `# Requirement coverage` and structuredContent holds {kind, data}.

items.title: Reports MCP tool failures as isError with a `CODE: message` text
items.description: If an MCP tool call fails, then overseer shall return an isError result whose text is the error code followed by the message.
acceptance_criteria: Given no item REQ-0099, when get_item is called with id REQ-0099, then isError is true and the text is `NOT_FOUND: No item with id REQ-0099.`
Given an unexpected exception inside a tool, when the call fails, then isError is true and the text is `INTERNAL: <message>`.

items.title: Annotates MCP tools with read-only, destructive and open-world hints
items.description: overseer shall annotate every MCP tool with readOnlyHint, destructiveHint and openWorldHint values that match the tool's effect on project data.
acceptance_criteria: Given the tool list, when a client reads find_similar, check_coverage, get_item, list_items, search or report, then readOnlyHint is true and openWorldHint is false.

Given the tool list, when a client reads create_item, update_item, link_items, export_report, import_items or open_board, then readOnlyHint is false, destructiveHint is false and openWorldHint is false.

items.title: Records the MCP client name as the channel of items and history events
items.description: When an MCP tool writes to the registry, overseer shall record the MCP client's name from initialize as the item's recorded_via and the history event's via.
acceptance_criteria: Given a client that initialized with name 'test-client', when it calls create_item, then the created item has recorded_via 'test-client'.
Given a client that sent no client info, when it writes an item, then recorded_via is 'mcp'.

items.title: Bounds MCP tool arguments: text length, result limits and list pagination
items.description: If an MCP tool argument falls outside its declared bounds, then overseer shall reject the call before touching the registry.
acceptance_criteria: Given find_similar, check_coverage or search, when text/query is empty or longer than 4000 characters, then the call is rejected.
Given find_similar or check_coverage, when limit is outside 1–20 (default 5), then the call is rejected; search accepts limit 1–50 (default 10).
Given list_items, when limit is outside 1–200 (default 50) or offset is negative (default 0), then the call is rejected; open_board accepts port 1–65535.

items.title: Publishes per-tool descriptions with result shapes and usage limits
items.description: overseer shall publish a description for every MCP tool that states its purpose, its result shape and its usage constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Given the tool list, when a client reads create_item, then the description names the {created:true…} and {created:false, reason:"possible_duplicate", candidates} results and asks to surface lint warnings.
Given the tool list, when a client reads export_report and import_items, then they say to export only when the user asks and that issue text is untrusted data limited to 100 issues per call.
Given the tool list, when a client reads the status argument of create_item, update_item or list_items, then it lists the valid statuses per kind.

items.title: Keeps stdout reserved for JSON-RPC while the MCP server runs
items.description: While the MCP server runs, overseer shall write only JSON-RPC messages to stdout.
acceptance_criteria: Given `overseer mcp` running, when overseer emits a warning, then it is written to stderr as `overseer: <message>` and stdout carries only JSON-RPC frames.
items.fit_criterion: 0 non-JSON-RPC bytes on stdout during an `overseer mcp` session; diagnostics go to stderr prefixed `overseer: ` (src/core/db.ts) and src/ contains no console.log calls.

items.title: Sends usage instructions to the MCP client at initialize
items.description: When an MCP client initializes, overseer shall send server instructions that tell the agent when and how to use the overseer tools.
acceptance_criteria: Given a connected MCP client, when it reads the server instructions, then they equal INSTRUCTIONS.

Given the instructions, when read, then they say to call find_similar before create_item, answer coverage questions with check_coverage, record text in the user's language and delegate bulk work to the overseer subagent.
Given the instructions, when read, then they say to retry with an absolute project_dir on NO_PROJECT and to stop using overseer on DISABLED without turning it on.

items.title: Reuses one open project service per resolved project root across MCP calls
items.description: While the MCP server runs, overseer shall reuse a single open service per resolved project root across tool calls.
acceptance_criteria: Given a create_item call that opened the project database, when a later call resolves to the same root, then the cached service is used and the on/off switch is still checked on that call.

items.title: Closes open databases and board servers when the MCP connection closes
items.description: When the MCP connection closes, overseer shall close every project database and web board server the session opened.
acceptance_criteria: Given an MCP session that opened two projects and one board, when the client disconnects, then both services are closed and the board server stops listening.

items.title: Identifies the MCP server as `overseer` with the package version
items.description: When an MCP client initializes, overseer shall report the server name `overseer` and the installed package version.
acceptance_criteria: Given a connected MCP client, when it reads serverInfo, then name is 'overseer' and version equals the package.json version.

items.title: Ships the overseer, overseer-bootstrap and overseer-import skills with their reference files
items.description: When overseer installs into a harness, overseer shall copy the overseer, overseer-bootstrap and overseer-import skill folders with content identical to its templates/skills files.
acceptance_criteria: Given an install for any target, when it finishes, then <skills dir>/overseer/SKILL.md, overseer/references/fields.md, overseer-bootstrap/SKILL.md and overseer-import/SKILL.md exist.
Given the skills were already installed with the same content, when install runs again, then every skill folder is reported unchanged and no file is rewritten.
Given templates/skills, when the skill test walks it, then it finds more markdown files than the three SKILL.md files (the reference files).

items.title: Skill frontmatter conforms to the Agent Skills format
items.description: overseer shall start every shipped SKILL.md with a YAML frontmatter block that holds only the name and description keys.
acceptance_criteria: Given each of overseer, overseer-bootstrap and overseer-import, when its SKILL.md is parsed, then it starts with '---\n' and the frontmatter keys are exactly description and name.
Given a skill folder, when its frontmatter is read, then name equals the folder name and matches ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$.
Given a skill description, when measured, then it is non-empty and at most 1024 characters long.
items.fit_criterion: '---' on line 1; frontmatter keys exactly {name, description}; name equals the folder name and matches ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$; description is a non-empty string of at most 1024 characters.

items.title: Skill makes agents run a duplicate check before creating any item
items.description: overseer shall instruct agents to call find_similar or check_coverage before every create_item call.
acceptance_criteria: Given an agent about to record an item, when it follows the overseer skill, then it calls find_similar with title plus description and kind requirement before create_item.
Given find_similar answers duplicate, when the agent follows the skill, then it does not create the item and shows the candidate instead.

Given create_item answers created:false with reason possible_duplicate, when the agent follows the skill, then it offers to update the existing item, create and link refines, or create anyway with allow_duplicate:true.

items.title: Export registry reports into a project-relative folder
items.description: When an export is requested, overseer shall write README.md, requirements.md, backlog.md, history.md and overseer.json into the output folder below the project root, creating the folder when it is missing.
acceptance_criteria: Given a populated registry, when exportReports runs without options, then it writes the five files into docs/overseer and returns out_dir 'docs/overseer' plus the five project-relative paths.
Given outDir 'reports/out' and only ['history'], when exportReports runs, then only reports/out/history.md is written.
Given an unknown part in only, when exportReports runs, then it fails with INVALID_INPUT.

items.title: Generated-file header on every Markdown export
items.description: overseer shall start every exported Markdown file with a comment naming the overseer-cli version and generation time and telling readers to regenerate it with "overseer export" instead of editing it.
acceptance_criteria: Given an export, when README.md, requirements.md, backlog.md and history.md are read, then line 1 matches '<!-- Generated by overseer-cli <version> on <ISO>. Do not edit; run "overseer export" to regenerate. -->'.

items.title: Deterministic export output for clean repository diffs
items.description: While the registry data is unchanged, overseer shall produce export files whose content differs between two runs only in the generation timestamps.
acceptance_criteria: Given a seeded registry, when exportReports runs twice, then all five files are equal once the header line and generated_at are removed.
items.fit_criterion: Two consecutive exports of the same data are identical after removing the '<!-- Generated by overseer-cli' header line and the overseer.json "generated_at" line; items are ordered by ID ascending and events by seq.

items.title: History export filtered by a since date, newest first
items.description: When an export is requested with a since date, overseer shall limit history.md to the events recorded at or after that date.
acceptance_criteria: Given events dated 2020-01-01 and since '2021-01-01', when history.md is exported, then it does not contain 2020-01-01 and states 'Events since 2021-01-01, newest first.'
Given since 'yesterday', when exportReports runs, then it fails with INVALID_INPUT (accepted forms: YYYY-MM-DD or ISO date-time).
Given a status change after a create event, when history.md is exported, then the status change is listed before the create event.

items.title: requirements.md export with per-requirement detail sections
items.description: When the requirements part is exported, overseer shall write requirements.md with a requirements table followed by one section per requirement listing its fields, statement, acceptance-criteria checklist, links and history.
acceptance_criteria: Given REQ-0001 implemented by US-0001, when requirements.md is read, then it contains '### REQ-0001 — Password reset by email' and '- implements ← US-0001 Reset forgotten password (story, in_progress)'.
Given a requirement with acceptance criteria, when requirements.md is read, then each criterion appears as a '- [ ] ' checklist line.

items.title: backlog.md export with board, epic tree and bugs
items.description: When the backlog part is exported, overseer shall write backlog.md with the board columns, the epic → story → task tree and a bugs table showing the items each bug affects.
acceptance_criteria: Given EPIC-0001 > US-0001 > TASK-0001, when backlog.md is read, then the tree lists them nested in that order with their statuses.
Given BUG-0001 affecting REQ-0001, when backlog.md is read, then it contains '| BUG-0001 | Reset link expired immediately | major | backlog | REQ-0001 |'.

items.title: Idempotent upsert of GitHub/GitLab issues by external reference
items.description: When a batch of GitHub or GitLab issues is imported, overseer shall create or update exactly one item per issue keyed by the external reference '<source>:<external_id>'.
acceptance_criteria: Given issue acme/demo#7 from github, when it is imported, then BUG-0001 is created with external_ref 'github:acme/demo#7'.
Given the same issue imported again unchanged, when import runs, then the result lists BUG-0001 under unchanged and nothing is created.
Given the same external_id twice in one batch, when import runs, then only the first entry is used and a warning is returned.

items.title: Import batch validated as a whole before any write
items.description: If any entry of an import batch fails validation, then overseer shall reject the whole batch with INVALID_INPUT without writing any item.
acceptance_criteria: Given a batch with one valid issue and one with state 'merged', when import runs, then it fails with INVALID_INPUT and the registry stays empty.
Given a batch with 0 or more than 100 items or a source other than github/gitlab, when import runs, then it fails with INVALID_INPUT.

items.title: Imported issue kind derived from type hint or labels
items.description: When an issue is imported for the first time, overseer shall take its kind from type_hint, otherwise from its labels, defaulting to task.
acceptance_criteria: Given labels Regression, epic, REQ, non-functional, enhancement or docs, when the kind is derived, then it is bug, epic, requirement, requirement, story or task respectively.
Given labels ['bug'] and type_hint 'story', when the kind is derived, then it is story.
Given labels ['requirement','performance'], when imported, then the requirement gets req_type non_functional (labels matching nfr, non-functional, performance or security).

items.title: Initial status of a newly imported item from issue state
items.description: When an issue is imported for the first time, overseer shall set the item status from the issue state, using implemented or done for closed issues.
acceptance_criteria: Given open issues, when imported, then requirements become approved, epics open and other kinds backlog, or in_progress when a label matches 'in progress', 'doing' or 'wip'.
Given closed issues, when imported, then requirements become implemented and other kinds done, with delivered_at set.
Given gitlab issues labelled [requirement,performance], [feature,WIP], [epic] closed and [] closed, when imported, then statuses are approved, in_progress, done and done.

items.title: Re-import refreshes remote fields and keeps local data
items.description: When an already imported issue is imported again, overseer shall overwrite only the title, description, tags, assignee, milestone and URL with the remote values, leaving locally maintained fields and links unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Given BUG-0001 with local priority must and an affects link to REQ-0001, when it is re-imported with a new title, then the title changes while priority and the link stay.
Given a changed remote field, when re-imported, then an update event via 'import:github' is recorded for that field and the item is listed under updated.

items.title: Last import time recorded per source and repository
items.description: When an import batch completes, overseer shall store the import time for its source and repository so that the summary report lists it.
acceptance_criteria: Given an import from github acme/demo, when lastImports is read, then it returns [{source:'github', repo:'acme/demo', at: <last_import_at of the result>}].

items.title: CLI import from a JSON file or standard input
items.description: When "overseer import <file|->" runs with --source and --repo, overseer shall read a JSON array of issues, or an object with an items array, from the file or from stdin for '-'.
acceptance_criteria: Given input that is not valid JSON, when overseer import runs, then it fails with INVALID_INPUT 'Import input is not valid JSON'.
Given a file path that does not exist, when overseer import runs, then it fails with INVALID_INPUT 'Import file not found'.
Given a JSON value that is neither an array nor an object with items, when overseer import runs, then it fails with INVALID_INPUT.

items.title: Every shipped skill markdown file ends with the managed-by marker
items.description: overseer shall end every markdown file under templates/skills with the line '<!-- managed-by: overseer-cli -->'.
acceptance_criteria: Given every markdown file under templates/skills, when read, then it ends with '<!-- managed-by: overseer-cli -->' or that line plus a newline.
Given templates/agent-prompt.md, when read, then it does not contain the marker and does not start with '---'.
items.fit_criterion: 100 % of *.md files under templates/skills end with '<!-- managed-by: overseer-cli -->' (optionally followed by one newline); templates/agent-prompt.md contains no marker (the marker is added when the agent file is rendered).

items.title: Export folder confined to the project root
items.description: If the export output folder resolves outside the project root, then overseer shall reject the export with INVALID_INPUT before writing any file.
acceptance_criteria: Given outDir '../outside', when exportReports runs, then it throws an error with code INVALID_INPUT.
items.fit_criterion: Absolute paths and paths whose relative form starts with '..' (e.g. '../outside') fail with code INVALID_INPUT; the same check applies when the export_dir config key is set.

items.title: Machine-readable overseer.json export
items.description: When the json part is exported, overseer shall write overseer.json with format 'overseer-export/1' containing the project name, the root folder name, every item, every link and every event.
acceptance_criteria: Given a seeded registry, when overseer.json is parsed, then format is 'overseer-export/1', items are listed by ID ascending and links holds every recorded link.

items.title: README.md export summarises the registry
items.description: When the summary part is exported, overseer shall write README.md with item counts, requirement coverage, open bugs by severity, drift findings, items changed in the last 14 days and links to the other exported files.
acceptance_criteria: Given a full export, when README.md is read, then it links '[requirements.md](requirements.md)'.

items.title: Imported item fields copied from the remote issue
items.description: When an issue is imported for the first time, overseer shall store its body as description, labels as tags, first assignee as assignee, milestone, and URL as source with no asked_by.
acceptance_criteria: Given issue acme/demo#7 labelled bug and assigned to octocat, when imported, then the item has tags ['bug'], assignee 'octocat', asked_by null, source equal to the issue URL and recorded_via 'import:github'.
Given a new imported item, when its history is read, then it has one 'import' event via 'import:github' whose new value is the external reference.
Given a body longer than 20000 characters, when imported, then the description is truncated to 20000 characters.

items.title: Status follows remote open/closed transitions only
items.description: When a re-imported issue's open/closed state differs from the stored remote state, overseer shall move the item to the status that matches the new remote state.
acceptance_criteria: Given BUG-0001 imported open, when it is re-imported closed, then its status becomes done, delivered_at is set and a status event is recorded.
Given the closed BUG-0001, when it is re-imported open, then its status becomes backlog and delivered_at is cleared.
Given an unchanged remote state, when re-imported, then the local status is left as it is.

items.title: Parent links resolved from parent_external_id
items.description: When an imported issue names a parent_external_id, overseer shall set its parent to the imported item with that reference if the parent rules allow it, otherwise leave the parent unset and return a warning.
acceptance_criteria: Given a story whose parent epic appears later in the same batch, when imported, then US-0001 gets parent EPIC-0001.
Given a parent that is not imported, when imported, then the warning 'TASK-0001: parent acme/demo#99 is not imported; parent left unset.' is returned.
Given a task whose parent is an epic, when imported, then the warning 'TASK-0002: a task cannot have a epic parent (EPIC-0001); parent left unset.' is returned.

items.title: Imported items flagged as possible duplicates of local items
items.description: When an import creates new items, overseer shall report each one that matches a non-imported item at related similarity or above as a possible duplicate without linking them.
acceptance_criteria: Given local BUG-0001 'Login fails on Safari', when the same issue is imported, then possible_duplicates is [{id:'BUG-0002', similar_to:[{id:'BUG-0001', similarity}]}] and no link is created.

items.title: Filter item lists by requirement coverage state
items.description: When list_items receives one or more coverage states, overseer shall return only the requirements whose derived coverage is one of those states.
acceptance_criteria: Given REQ-0001 implemented by a backlog story and a rejected REQ-0002, when the list is filtered by coverage tracked, then only REQ-0001 is returned with coverage tracked

items.title: Drift report flags requirement statuses that contradict their implementing work
items.description: When the drift report is requested, overseer shall list each requirement whose status contradicts the status of its non-cancelled implementing items, with the drift rule, the work items and a suggested action.
acceptance_criteria: Given an approved or proposed requirement whose live implementing items are all done, when report drift runs, then it is listed with rule work_done_status_open
Given an implemented or verified requirement with a live implementing item not done, when report drift runs, then it is listed with rule status_ahead_of_work
Given a proposed requirement with a live implementing item in in_progress, review or done, when report drift runs, then it is listed with rule unapproved_in_progress

items.title: Return lint warnings on requirement and story writes without blocking them
items.description: When a requirement or story is created or updated, overseer shall return its lint warnings, each with rule, severity (warn or info) and message, while still saving the write.
acceptance_criteria: Given a non-functional requirement 'The API shall be fast.' without category or fit criterion, when it is created, then created is true and the warnings are nfr_category_missing, nfr_not_measurable and vague_term
Given an epic, task or bug, when it is created or updated, then no lint warnings are returned

items.title: Lint flags vague English and Spanish wording
items.description: If the title or description of a requirement or story contains a term from the vague-term list, then overseer shall return a vague_term warning naming each matched term.
acceptance_criteria: Given the description 'El sistema deberá ser rápido y/o fácil', when the requirement is created, then a vague_term warning names "rápido", "y/o" and "fácil"
Given the title 'Fast API', when it is created, then a vague_term warning is returned; terms match case-insensitively on whole words only

items.title: Lint flags requirements that bundle several shall statements
items.description: If a requirement description contains more than one modal verb from the requirement-statement list, then overseer shall return a multiple_requirements warning.
acceptance_criteria: Given the description 'The system shall log in. The system must log out.', when the requirement is created, then a multiple_requirements warning reports 2 statements
Given the modal-verb list in src/core/lint-terms.ts (shall, must, debe, deberá), when a description holds exactly one of them, then no multiple_requirements warning is returned

items.title: Lint flags missing acceptance criteria once an item leaves its first status
items.description: If a requirement past proposed or a story past backlog has no acceptance criteria, then overseer shall return a missing_acceptance_criteria warning.
acceptance_criteria: Given an approved requirement without acceptance criteria, when it is created, then a missing_acceptance_criteria warning is returned
Given a story without acceptance criteria, when its status changes to ready, then a missing_acceptance_criteria warning is returned; a proposed requirement or backlog story gets none

items.title: Summary report gives a project health overview
items.description: When the summary report is requested, overseer shall return the project name and root, item counts per kind and status, requirement counts per coverage state, open bugs per severity, the drift count, the last imports and whether semantic search is available.
acceptance_criteria: Given an approved requirement implemented by an in_progress story and an open major bug, when report summary runs, then counts.requirement.approved is 1, coverage.in_progress is 1 and open_bugs_by_severity.major is 1
Given sqlite-vec is unavailable, when report summary runs, then the markdown states search is keyword only

items.title: Traceability report maps each requirement to its work and affecting bugs
items.description: When the traceability report is requested, overseer shall show for each requirement its implementing stories and tasks, their child items and the bugs that affect it.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requirement implemented by a story with a child task and affected by a major bug, when report traceability runs, then implemented_by lists the story with children [TASK-0001] and affected_by lists BUG-0001 with severity major

items.title: Derive requirement coverage from linked work at read time
items.description: When a requirement is read, overseer shall derive its coverage state from the requirement status, its backlog flag and the non-cancelled items that implement it.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requirement with no implementing items and not in the backlog, when it is read, then its coverage is untracked; after setting in_backlog it is tracked

Given a requirement whose live implementing items include one in review or in_progress, when it is read, then its coverage is in_progress; when all live implementing items are done (cancelled ones ignored), then it is delivered
Given a requirement with status implemented, verified or deferred/rejected/obsolete, when it is read, then its coverage is delivered, verified or not_applicable respectively

items.title: Attach derived coverage to every requirement returned by item and similarity queries
items.description: When get_item, list_items, find_similar or check_coverage returns a requirement, overseer shall include the requirement's derived coverage state in the result.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requirement implemented by an in_progress story, when get_item returns it, then item.coverage is in_progress
Given requirements in the registry, when find_similar or check_coverage matches a requirement, then the match carries its coverage state

items.title: Lint flags non-functional requirements without a measurable target
items.description: If a non-functional requirement has no fit criterion and its description contains no digit, then overseer shall return an nfr_not_measurable warning.
acceptance_criteria: Given a non-functional requirement 'The API shall be fast.' without fit criterion, when it is created, then an nfr_not_measurable warning is returned
Given a non-functional requirement with category performance_efficiency and description 'p95 under 300 ms', when it is created, then no warning is returned

items.title: Lint flags non-functional requirements without an ISO 25010 category
items.description: If a non-functional requirement has no nfr_category, then overseer shall return an nfr_category_missing warning.
acceptance_criteria: Given a non-functional requirement created without nfr_category, when it is created, then an nfr_category_missing warning is returned

items.title: Lint flags stories not written in the role-goal-benefit template
items.description: If a story description matches neither "As a … I want … so that" nor "Como … quiero … para", then overseer shall return a story_format warning with severity info.
acceptance_criteria: Given a story described 'Reset the password', when it is updated, then a story_format warning with severity info is returned

Given the description 'Como usuario quiero restablecer mi clave para recuperar el acceso' or 'As an admin I want to reset passwords so that users regain access', when it is updated with acceptance criteria, then no warning is returned

items.title: Lint flags requirement and story titles over 100 characters
items.description: If a requirement or story title is longer than 100 characters, then overseer shall return a title_too_long warning stating the title length.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requirement titled with 101 characters, when it is created, then a title_too_long warning is returned

items.title: Lint report lists warnings for every open requirement and story
items.description: When the lint report is requested, overseer shall list the lint warnings of every requirement and story that is not in a closed status, with item ID, title, rule, severity and message.
acceptance_criteria: Given an approved requirement and an in_progress story without acceptance criteria and a non-template story description, when report lint runs, then it lists REQ:missing_acceptance_criteria, US:missing_acceptance_criteria and US:story_format

items.title: Coverage report lists every requirement with its coverage and implementing items
items.description: When the coverage report is requested, overseer shall list every requirement with its type, priority, status, coverage state and implementing items.
acceptance_criteria: Given an approved requirement implemented by an in_progress story, when report coverage runs, then its row has coverage in_progress and implemented_by lists the story with status in_progress

items.title: Board report groups stories, tasks and bugs into workflow columns
items.description: When the board report is requested, overseer shall group stories, tasks and bugs into the columns backlog, ready, in_progress, review and done, showing each card's kind, title, priority, assignee and implemented requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Given an in_progress story implementing a requirement, when report board runs, then the columns are backlog, ready, in_progress, review, done and the in_progress column holds the story card with implements [REQ id]

items.description: If no harness is selected or detected, then overseer install shall fail with an INVALID_INPUT error asking for --targets.
acceptance_criteria: Given an empty home and no harness executable on PATH, when "install --dry-run --json" runs, then the exit code is 1 and the error is INVALID_INPUT with a message containing "--targets"
Given a terminal with nothing preselected, when the user presses Enter, then the same INVALID_INPUT error is returned

items.title: --targets picks harnesses without detection or the prompt
items.description: When --targets is given, overseer install shall install for exactly the listed harnesses without running detection or the prompt.
acceptance_criteria: Given "install --dry-run --scope project --targets claude --json", when it runs, then the report targets are [claude]
Given "--targets vim", when install runs, then the exit code is 1 and the error code is INVALID_INPUT
Given an empty --targets list, when install runs, then it fails with INVALID_INPUT "--targets needs at least one of claude, omp, codex, gemini, copilot, cursor, opencode"

items.title: Pick the project start directory from argument, environment, client root or current directory
items.description: When a tool call or project command needs the project, overseer shall take the start directory from the first set source in the order: project_dir argument or --project flag, OVERSEER_PROJECT, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, the first file:// root advertised by the MCP client, the current directory.
acceptance_criteria: Given a repository and a shell in another directory, when `overseer add … --project <repo>` runs, then the item is recorded in that repository's registry and `overseer list --project <repo>` returns it

Given an MCP client advertising the root <repo>/packages/app (re-read after roots/list_changed) and a server started in the home directory, when create_item is called without project_dir, then <repo>/.overseer/overseer.db is created
Given a start directory that does not exist, when the project is resolved, then the call fails with INVALID_INPUT 'Project directory does not exist: <dir>'

items.title: Map git worktrees and subfolders to the main checkout as project root
items.description: When the start directory lies inside a git repository, overseer shall use the root of the repository's main checkout as the project root.
acceptance_criteria: Given a linked worktree of a repository, when the project is resolved from the worktree or one of its subfolders, then the root is the main checkout
Given a subfolder of the main checkout or a git submodule, when the project is resolved, then the root is the main checkout or, for the submodule, its top-level folder
Given git does not answer within 5 s, when the project is resolved, then overseer falls back to the lookup used outside git

items.title: Outside git, use the nearest ancestor holding .overseer/ as project root
items.description: If the start directory is not inside a git repository, then overseer shall use the nearest ancestor folder holding a .overseer/ folder as the project root, falling back to the start directory itself.
acceptance_criteria: Given <base>/proj/.overseer/ outside git, when the project is resolved from <base>/proj/a/b, then the root is <base>/proj
Given no .overseer/ in any ancestor of <base>/other/x outside git, when the project is resolved from it, then the root is <base>/other/x

items.title: Refuse writes when the project resolves to the home directory or filesystem root
items.description: If the resolved project root is the filesystem root, the home directory or an ancestor of the home directory, then overseer shall refuse every write with NO_PROJECT.
acceptance_criteria: Given an MCP server started in the home directory, when create_item is called without project_dir, then it answers 'NO_PROJECT: No project detected (resolved to <home>). Run inside a project folder, or pass project_dir / --project.' and <home>/.overseer does not exist
Given only a repository below home is turned on, when a write resolves to home, then NO_PROJECT is answered instead of DISABLED and the retry with project_dir <repo> creates the item
Given the project resolves to a guarded folder, when overseer init, enable, disable or install --scope project runs, then it fails with NO_PROJECT

items.title: Create the .overseer/ data folder on the first write to a project
items.description: When the first write reaches a turned-on project without a registry, overseer shall create the registry at <root>/.overseer/overseer.db.
acceptance_criteria: Given a repository without .overseer/, when the database is opened for writing, then <repo>/.overseer/overseer.db exists
Given a turned-on project without .overseer/, when overseer add, overseer init, overseer board or an MCP write tool runs, then .overseer/ is created
Given a repository without .overseer/, when a read command or read tool runs, then no .overseer/ folder is created

items.title: Answer reads on an uninitialized project with initialized:false and its root
items.description: When a read reaches a project without a registry, overseer shall answer {initialized: false, root} instead of an error.
acceptance_criteria: Given a turned-on repository without .overseer/, when `overseer list --json` runs, then it exits 0 and prints {"initialized": false, "root": <repo>}
Given a turned-on repository without .overseer/, when list_items is called over MCP, then the result is {initialized: false, root: <repo>}
Given the project resolves to the home directory, when a read runs, then it answers {initialized: false, root: <home>}

items.title: Keep the data folder git-ignored without editing the project's own files
items.description: overseer shall keep its data folder ignored by git through a .overseer/.gitignore file whose only rule is *.
acceptance_criteria: Given a clean repository, when the database is first opened for writing, then .overseer/.gitignore reads '*\n', <repo>/.gitignore does not exist and `git status --porcelain` is empty
items.fit_criterion: `.overseer/.gitignore` content is exactly `*\n` (rewritten when it differs); no `<root>/.gitignore` is created or edited; `git status --porcelain` stays empty after the first write in a clean repository.

items.title: Off by default: answer DISABLED until the user turns the project on
items.description: While no enable rule covers the project root, overseer shall answer every MCP tool call and every project CLI command with DISABLED.
acceptance_criteria: Given a repository with no rule, when `overseer add` runs from its src folder, then it exits 1 with DISABLED 'overseer is off for <repo> (overseer is off by default and works only in projects the user turned on). Do not use overseer in this project; to turn it on, the user runs: overseer enable --project <repo>' and the repository still holds only .git and src
Given a project that is off, when create_item, list_items or open_board is called over MCP, then each answers 'DISABLED: …' and no .overseer/ is created
Given an MCP server holding a cached service for a turned-on project, when the user config changes to turn it off, then the next tool call answers DISABLED

items.title: overseer enable records the project in the user's enabled_projects list
items.description: When the user runs overseer enable, overseer shall turn the project on by recording its root in enabled_projects of the user config file.
acceptance_criteria: Given an off repository, when `overseer enable` runs, then it prints 'overseer is now on for <repo> and every folder below it.', the config holds {enabled_projects: [<repo>], disabled_projects: []} and the repository still holds only .git and src
Given an enabled repository, when `overseer add` runs from a subfolder, then it exits 0
Given an enabled repository, when `overseer enable` runs again, then it prints 'overseer is already on for <repo>.' and reports changed: false

items.title: overseer disable turns the project off and keeps its existing registry
items.description: When the user runs overseer disable, overseer shall turn the project off without deleting its .overseer/ folder.
acceptance_criteria: Given an enabled repository with .overseer/, when `overseer disable` runs, then it prints 'Existing data in <repo>/.overseer is kept' and `overseer list` answers DISABLED
Given a repository enabled only by its own rule, when `overseer disable` runs, then the config returns to {enabled_projects: [], disabled_projects: []}
Given an off repository, when `overseer disable` runs, then it prints 'overseer is already off for <repo>.'

items.title: The closest enable or disable folder rule decides for nested projects
items.description: When several enable or disable rules cover a project root, overseer shall apply the rule of the closest covering folder, counting a folder listed in both lists as off.
acceptance_criteria: Given <work> enabled and <work>/client disabled, when `overseer add task` runs in <work>/client, then it answers DISABLED 'overseer is off for <client>. …', while in <work>/app it exits 0
Given <work> enabled, when `overseer enable` runs in <work>/app, then it prints 'overseer is already on for <app> (through <work>).'
Given a folder listed in both enabled_projects and disabled_projects, when a tool call reaches it, then it answers DISABLED

items.title: Re-enabling a disabled exception only removes that exception rule
items.description: When enable or disable runs on a folder whose ancestor rule already yields the requested state, overseer shall remove the folder's own opposite rule without adding a new rule.
acceptance_criteria: Given <work> enabled and <work>/client disabled, when `overseer enable` runs in <work>/client, then it prints 'overseer is now on for <client> (through <work>)' and the config holds {enabled_projects: [<work>], disabled_projects: []}

items.title: Store the on/off rules in the per-OS user config folder
items.description: overseer shall store the on/off rules in a config.json file inside the operating system's per-user configuration folder.
acceptance_criteria: Given OVERSEER_CONFIG_DIR=<dir>, when `overseer enable` runs, then <dir>/config.json holds the enabled_projects and disabled_projects lists
items.fit_criterion: Linux `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/overseer/config.json`; macOS `~/Library/Application Support/overseer/config.json`; Windows `%APPDATA%\overseer\config.json`; `OVERSEER_CONFIG_DIR` replaces the folder; keys `enabled_projects` and `disabled_projects` hold absolute folder paths.

items.title: overseer init and install --scope project also turn the project on
items.description: When the user runs overseer init or a non-dry-run overseer install --scope project, overseer shall turn the project on in the user config.
acceptance_criteria: Given an off repository, when `overseer init` runs, then it prints 'overseer is now on for <repo>' and `overseer add` then exits 0
Given an off repository, when `overseer install --scope project --dry-run` runs, then it prints 'would turn overseer on for <repo>' and `overseer list` still answers DISABLED
Given an off repository, when `overseer install --scope project --json` runs, then the output holds project {root: <repo>, enabled: true, changed: true} and `overseer list` exits 0

items.title: Fail with CONFIG_PARSE on a malformed user config instead of reading it as empty
items.description: If the user config file is not valid JSON or breaks its schema, then overseer shall fail with CONFIG_PARSE naming the file.
acceptance_criteria: Given config.json holds '{ "enabled_projects": [', when `overseer list --json` runs, then it exits 1 with error code CONFIG_PARSE and a message containing the config.json path
items.fit_criterion: Every project CLI command, enable/disable and MCP tool call exits 1 (or isError) with code CONFIG_PARSE and the config.json path in the message; a malformed file is never treated as empty.

items.title: Install downloads the embedding model unless --skip-model or --dry-run
items.description: When overseer install finishes without --skip-model or --dry-run, overseer shall download and load the embedding model into the local model cache.
acceptance_criteria: Given --dry-run, when "install --scope project --targets claude --json" runs, then the JSON report has no model field
Given --skip-model, when install runs, then no model download is attempted
Given a successful download, when install prints its report, then it shows "Model Xenova/multilingual-e5-small ready in <cache dir>" (with --json: model {ready: true, message})

items.title: Skill teaches board conventions for epics, INVEST stories, tasks and bugs
items.description: When an agent plans work on the board, overseer shall instruct it to link each story or task to the requirements it delivers with an implements relation.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new story, when the agent follows the overseer skill, then its description reads 'As a <role> I want <goal> so that <benefit>' (or 'Como <rol> quiero <objetivo> para <beneficio>'), parent_id is an epic, it has Given/When/Then criteria and links [{rel: implements, to: REQ-…}].

Given a bug, when the agent records it, then it sets bug_details {steps[], expected, actual, environment?}, a severity of critical, major, minor or trivial, and an affects link to a requirement or story.
Given a grooming request, when the agent follows the skill, then it uses report board, report lint and list_items with coverage [untracked].

items.title: Skill teaches the after-implementing flow: close work, delivered_in, code_refs, drift check
items.description: When an agent finishes implementing tracked work, overseer shall instruct it to run report drift and resolve each finding.
acceptance_criteria: Given finished work, when the agent follows the skill, then it moves work items to review or done with a comment, sets delivered_in (release, PR URL or commit) and code_refs, and sets the requirement to implemented (or verified once its verification method passed).

Given drift findings work_done_status_open, status_ahead_of_work or unapproved_in_progress, when the agent follows the skill, then it resolves each one and asks the user for approval on unapproved_in_progress.

items.title: Agents export docs/overseer/ only when the user asks
items.description: overseer shall instruct agents to call export_report only after the user asks for an export.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user who asks for an export, when the agent follows the skill, then it calls export_report (default docs/overseer/: README.md, requirements.md, backlog.md, history.md, overseer.json) and suggests committing the folder.
Given no export request, when the subagent or overseer-bootstrap finishes, then it writes no export and at most offers one.

items.title: Subagent prompt is rendered per harness with its skill path and tool prefix
items.description: When overseer writes the subagent file for a harness, overseer shall replace the {{SKILL_PATH}} and {{TOOL_PREFIX}} placeholders of templates/agent-prompt.md with that harness's values.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user-scope install of all targets, when the agent files are read, then they contain mcp__overseer__find_similar (Claude Code, Codex), mcp__overseer_find_similar (OMP), mcp_overseer_find_similar (Gemini CLI), overseer-find_similar (Copilot CLI), overseer_find_similar (OpenCode) and (harness-specific)find_similar (Cursor).

Given a user-scope install, when the Claude Code agent file is read, then it contains the absolute path <home>/.claude/skills/overseer/SKILL.md; given a project-scope install, the Codex agent contains the project-relative .agents/skills/overseer/SKILL.md.
Given any rendered markdown agent, when read, then it starts with '---' frontmatter, contains no '{{' and ends with '<!-- managed-by: overseer-cli -->'.

items.title: Subagent reads the overseer skill before anything else
items.description: When the overseer subagent starts a task, overseer shall instruct it to read and follow the overseer skill before any other step.
acceptance_criteria: Given the rendered subagent prompt, when read, then its First step points to the installed overseer SKILL.md path.
Given a bootstrapping task or a GitHub/GitLab import, when the subagent starts, then the prompt tells it to also follow overseer-bootstrap or overseer-import from the sibling skill folders.
Given the Gemini CLI agent file, when read, then its body starts with 'Call activate_skill for `overseer` first'.

items.title: Install places each harness's skills, subagent and MCP entry at its scope-specific locations
items.description: When the user runs `overseer install`, overseer shall write the overseer skill folders, the overseer subagent file and the overseer MCP server entry at the locations defined for each selected harness in the chosen scope.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user-scope install for a single target, when install runs, then exactly that target's files are written under HOME (e.g. omp: .omp/agent/agents/overseer.md, .omp/agent/mcp.json and .omp/agent/skills/{overseer,overseer-bootstrap,overseer-import}).

Given `--scope project` and all seven targets, when install runs, then the project tree equals test/fixtures/install/golden-project.json (e.g. .mcp.json, .github/agents/overseer.agent.md, .codex/config.toml, opencode.json) and nothing is written under HOME.
Given only opencode.jsonc exists in the OpenCode config folder, when install runs for opencode, then opencode.jsonc is edited and no opencode.json is created.

items.title: Installer never creates or edits harness instruction files such as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md
items.description: overseer shall limit install writes to the skill folders, the subagent file, the MCP config file and its backups for each selected harness.
acceptance_criteria: Given an empty HOME or project, when install runs for one target in either scope, then the created file list equals that target's expected skill, agent and MCP config paths.
items.fit_criterion: For each of the 7 targets × 2 scopes, a single-target install creates exactly the paths listed in EXPECTED_FILES of test/install.test.ts; no AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md or other instruction file is created or modified.

items.title: MCP launch command uses absolute node + cli.js in user scope and `overseer mcp` in project scope
items.description: When overseer writes its MCP server entry, overseer shall launch the server with the absolute Node binary and absolute dist/cli.js path plus `mcp` in user scope, and with the command `overseer mcp` in project scope.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user-scope install, when the entries are written, then omp and cursor hold {type: stdio, command: <node>, args: [<cli.js>, 'mcp']}, gemini adds timeout 120000, copilot uses type local with tools ['*'], codex adds startup_timeout_sec 30 and tool_timeout_sec 120, and opencode uses command [<node>, <cli.js>, 'mcp'].

Given a project-scope install, when the entries are written, then .mcp.json holds {type: stdio, command: 'overseer', args: ['mcp']} and .cursor/mcp.json holds args ['mcp', '--project', '${workspaceFolder}'].
Given an omp entry installed with an older cli.js path, when install runs with a new path, then the entry is updated in place and reported as updated.

items.title: Claude Code user-scope MCP server registered through the claude CLI
items.description: While installing for Claude Code in user scope, overseer shall register its MCP server by running `claude mcp remove --scope user overseer` followed by `claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio overseer -- <node> <cli.js> mcp`.
acceptance_criteria: Given claude on PATH and no registration, when install runs, then claude receives `mcp get overseer`, `mcp remove --scope user overseer` (failure ignored) and the `mcp add` command; a second install only calls `mcp get overseer` and reports unchanged.
Given a registration pointing to another node or cli.js, when install runs, then it is replaced and reported as updated.

Given claude is not on PATH, when install runs, then a 'manual' action shows the exact `claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio overseer -- <node> <cli.js> mcp` command and a warning is emitted.

items.title: Existing agent files and skill folders without the managed-by marker are skipped unless --force
items.description: If an existing subagent file or skill folder lacks the `managed-by: overseer-cli` marker, then overseer shall leave it untouched with a NOT_MANAGED warning unless `--force` is given.
acceptance_criteria: Given ~/.cursor/agents/overseer.md without the marker, when install runs without --force, then it is reported skipped (NOT_MANAGED), its content is unchanged and the cursor MCP entry is still written.
Given the same file, when install runs with --force, then it is overwritten with the marked agent and the previous content is kept in overseer.md.overseer-backup.
Given an unmanaged ~/.claude/skills/overseer/SKILL.md, when install and then uninstall run, then the file is unchanged.

items.title: JSON/JSONC harness configs keep other keys, comments and formatting around the overseer entry
items.description: When overseer adds or removes its entry in an existing JSON or JSONC harness config, overseer shall leave every other key, comment and formatting detail of the file unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Given ~/.gemini/settings.json with comments and another server, when install runs, then the comments and the other entry remain, an overseer entry is added and no $schema key is inserted.
Given that installed file, when uninstall runs, then the file is reported updated and its text equals the original.
items.fit_criterion: Install then uninstall of gemini over a settings.json with // and /* */ comments and another server restores the original text byte for byte; `$schema` is inserted only when overseer creates the file.

items.title: Serve the web board on the loopback interface
items.description: When the user runs `overseer board` or an agent calls the open_board tool, overseer shall serve the web board over HTTP on 127.0.0.1 at the requested port, else at the board_port setting (default 4477).
acceptance_criteria: Given a turned-on project with board_port 4477, when the user runs `overseer board --no-open`, then overseer prints `overseer board: http://127.0.0.1:4477/ (Ctrl+C to stop)` and serves until SIGINT or SIGTERM.
Given `overseer board --port 5000` or open_board {port: 5000}, when the board starts, then it listens on 127.0.0.1:5000 and returns http://127.0.0.1:5000/.
Given a turned-on project without .overseer/, when the board starts, then the data folder is created first (write mode, home guard answers NO_PROJECT).

items.title: Fall back to the next free port when the board port is taken
items.description: If the requested board port is already in use, then overseer shall try the following ports one at a time, up to 19 ports above the requested one, before reporting the error.
acceptance_criteria: Given port 4477 is in use, when the board starts with the default port, then it listens on the first free port from 4478 to 4496 and returns that URL.
Given ports 4477 to 4496 are all in use, when the board starts, then the EADDRINUSE error is reported and no server keeps running.
Given a listen error other than EADDRINUSE, when the board starts, then the error is reported without trying another port.

items.title: Reuse the running board on repeated open_board calls
items.description: While a board started by the MCP server is running for a project, overseer shall answer further open_board calls for that project with the URL of the running board.
acceptance_criteria: Given open_board already started a board for project P in this MCP server process, when open_board is called again for P, then it returns the same {url} without starting a second server.
Given open_board is called for a different project Q, when no board runs for Q, then a separate board is started for Q.

items.title: Open the board in the system browser on start
items.description: When the board starts with browser opening enabled, overseer shall launch the system browser at the board URL followed by `#/board`.
acceptance_criteria: Given Linux, when the board starts without --no-open, then `xdg-open http://127.0.0.1:<port>/#/board` is spawned detached (macOS `open`, Windows `cmd /c start`).
Given the opener command is missing or fails, when the board starts, then the board keeps running and the URL is still printed or returned.
Given `overseer board --no-open` or open_board {open_browser: false}, when the board starts, then no browser is launched.

items.title: Reject board requests whose Host header is not the loopback address
items.description: If a board HTTP request carries a Host header other than `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>`, then overseer shall answer it with HTTP 403 and error code FORBIDDEN.
acceptance_criteria: Given the board on port 4477, when GET /api/project arrives with Host evil.example:4477, then the response is 403 {error:{code:'FORBIDDEN'}}.
Given the board on port 4477, when GET /api/project arrives with Host 127.0.0.1:9999, then the response is 403.
Given the board on port 4477, when GET /api/project arrives with Host localhost:4477, then the response is 200.
items.fit_criterion: Every request (API and static) whose Host is not exactly 127.0.0.1:<listening port> or localhost:<listening port> receives HTTP 403 before any handler runs.

items.title: Require the per-start token on mutating board requests
items.description: If a board request with a method other than GET or HEAD lacks an X-Overseer-Token header equal to the token generated at board start, then overseer shall reject it with HTTP 403.
acceptance_criteria: Given a running board, when PATCH /api/items/TASK-0001 is sent without X-Overseer-Token, then the response is 403.
Given a running board, when PATCH /api/items/TASK-0001 is sent with X-Overseer-Token 'nope', then the response is 403; with the right token it is 200.
Given GET /, when index.html is served, then `<!--OVERSEER_BOOT-->` is replaced by `<script>window.__OVERSEER__={token:"<token>"}</script>` and the SPA sends that token on every non-GET request.
items.fit_criterion: Token = 24 bytes from crypto.randomBytes as 48 hex characters, regenerated on every board start; 100% of POST/PATCH/DELETE requests without the exact token get 403 FORBIDDEN.

items.title: Confine board static file serving to the built web assets
items.description: overseer shall serve board static files only from inside the built web assets folder.
acceptance_criteria: Given a running board, when GET /assets/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd is requested, then the response does not contain the file (the SPA index is returned instead).
Given GET /assets/app.js, when served, then the content-type is text/javascript and the cache-control is `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; index.html is served with `no-store`.
Given the web assets are not built, when a non-API page is requested, then the response is 503 'Board assets are not built (run "npm run build" in the overseer package).'
items.fit_criterion: Only regular files whose resolved path starts with <dist/web>/ are read; any other non-API GET path returns index.html or 503.

items.title: Expose registry operations to the board as a JSON API
items.description: overseer shall expose the registry operations to the web board as JSON endpoints under /api for project info, item listing, item detail, create, update, link, unlink, search, similar items, reports and export.
acceptance_criteria: Given a running board, when POST /api/items creates a requirement, then the response is {created:true, item:{id:'REQ-0001', recorded_via:'web'}} and the same request again returns {created:false, reason:'possible_duplicate'}.

Given GET /api/items?kind=widget, GET /api/reports/nope or a requirement without req_type, when requested, then the response is 400 {error:{code:'INVALID_INPUT'}}; an unknown item gives 404 and an unknown /api route gives 404 NOT_FOUND.
Given GET /api/items without limit, when requested, then at most 1000 items are returned (limit 1-5000, offset, comma-separated status and coverage filters, include_closed=1).

items.title: Stream registry change events to board clients
items.description: When the registry database changes from any connection or process, overseer shall send a `changed` server-sent event to every client connected to /api/events.
acceptance_criteria: Given a client connected to /api/events, when another OverseerService connection commits a new task, then the stream contains `event: changed` with data {"data_version":N}.
Given a new connection to /api/events, when it opens, then the first event is `ready` with the current data_version and a `ping` event follows every 15 s without changes.
Given at least one connected client, when the board runs, then PRAGMA data_version is polled every 1000 ms on a dedicated read connection, which closes when the last client leaves.

items.title: Refresh open board pages on live change events
items.description: When the board page receives a `changed` event, overseer shall reload the data shown on every open board view.
acceptance_criteria: Given the board open in a browser, when an item is changed from the CLI or an agent, then the visible page refetches its data without a manual reload.
Given the event stream drops, when the header renders, then it shows a red 'Offline' indicator; on reconnect it shows a green 'Live' indicator and refetches all data once.

items.title: Show stories, tasks and bugs on a kanban by work status
items.description: overseer shall display the open stories, tasks and bugs on the #/board page in one column per work status from backlog to done.
acceptance_criteria: Given items of every kind, when #/board opens, then the columns Backlog, Ready, In progress, Review and Done hold stories, tasks and bugs only; requirements, epics and cancelled items are not shown.
Given a card, when it renders, then it shows the ID link, kind badge, title, priority badge, @assignee and the IDs of implemented requirements; clicking it opens #/items/<id>.
Given the kind, epic (direct children and grandchildren), tag and ID/title text filters, when set, then only matching cards remain; unknown hash routes open #/board.

items.title: Hide done cards older than 30 days unless requested
items.description: While the 'Show all done' option is unchecked, overseer shall hide from the Done column the cards whose status changed more than 30 days ago.
acceptance_criteria: Given a story done 40 days ago, when #/board opens, then the card is hidden and the Done column footer reads '1 done more than 30 days ago hidden'.
Given 'Show all done' is checked, when the board renders, then every done card is shown.

items.title: Change work-item status by dragging a card to another column
items.description: When the user drops a board card on a different column, overseer shall set the item status to the status of that column.
acceptance_criteria: Given US-0001 in Backlog, when its card is dragged to In progress, then the card moves at once and PATCH /api/items/US-0001 {status:'in_progress'} is sent.
Given the PATCH fails, when the error returns, then the card goes back to its previous column and an error toast 'Could not move <id> to <status>: <CODE>: <message>' appears.
Given a card dropped on its own column, when the drag ends, then no request is sent.

items.title: List requirements in a filterable table
items.description: overseer shall list the requirements on the #/requirements page in a table filterable by type, status, coverage and priority.
acceptance_criteria: Given #/requirements, when it opens, then each row shows ID, title, type, NFR category, priority, status, coverage, in backlog, asked by and created date.
Given the type, status, coverage or priority filter is set, when the table renders, then only matching rows remain and the count shows 'N shown'.
Given rejected or obsolete requirements, when no status filter is set, then they appear only with 'Show rejected/obsolete' checked.

items.title: Search requirements semantically from the requirements page
items.description: When the user stops typing in the requirements search box for 300 ms, overseer shall show the matching requirements ranked by similarity.
acceptance_criteria: Given the query 'password', when typing stops for 300 ms, then GET /api/search?q=password&kind=requirement&limit=100 runs and the rows gain a Similarity column in percent.
Given semantic search is unavailable, when results arrive, then the page notes 'keyword search only' and the header shows 'Keyword search only'.

items.title: Edit item fields from the item detail page
items.description: When the user saves the item detail form, overseer shall update the item with the fields whose values differ from the stored item.
acceptance_criteria: Given #/items/REQ-0001 with only the title edited, when Save is pressed, then PATCH sends only {title}, a toast 'Saved REQ-0001' lists 'Changed: title' and returned lint warnings are shown.
Given an empty title, a requirement without type or a non-numeric estimate, when Save is pressed, then the form shows the problem and sends nothing.
Given an item page, when it opens, then it shows ID, kind, status, coverage badge for requirements, created/updated/status-since dates, recorded via, external reference link and child items.

items.title: Install exits with code 1 when the model download fails
items.description: If the embedding model download after installation fails, then overseer install shall report the download failure with exit code 1.
acceptance_criteria: Given the download fails without --json, when install finishes, then stderr shows "error: model download failed: <cause>" and the exit code is 1
Given the download fails with --json, when install finishes, then the JSON report includes model {ready: false, message: "model download failed: <cause>"} and the exit code is 1

items.title: doctor flags a Node.js version below 22.13 as FAIL
items.description: If the running Node.js version is below 22.13, then overseer doctor shall report the node check as FAIL with the required minimum version.
acceptance_criteria: Given Node.js 22.12.0, when overseer doctor runs, then it prints "FAIL  node: 22.12.0 (need >= 22.13)"
Given the test runtime (Node ≥ 22.13), when "doctor --json" runs, then the node check status is OK

items.title: Warn when an item changes elsewhere during editing
items.description: If the item changes elsewhere while its detail form has unsaved edits, then overseer shall keep the user's draft and show a notice offering to discard it.
acceptance_criteria: Given unsaved edits on US-0001, when another process updates US-0001, then the notice 'This item was changed elsewhere while you were editing.' with 'Discard my changes' appears and the draft is kept.
Given no unsaved edits, when the item changes elsewhere, then the form shows the new values.

items.title: doctor probes sqlite-vec with an in-memory vec0 table
items.description: If sqlite-vec cannot load or create a vec0 table in an in-memory database, then overseer doctor shall report the sqlite check as WARN stating that only keyword search is available.
acceptance_criteria: Given sqlite-vec loads, when overseer doctor runs, then the sqlite check is OK with "node:sqlite <version> + sqlite-vec <version>"
Given sqlite-vec fails to load, when overseer doctor runs, then the sqlite check is WARN "sqlite-vec failed to load; keyword search only"
Given node:sqlite itself cannot open a database, when overseer doctor runs, then the sqlite check is FAIL "node:sqlite unavailable: <cause>"

items.title: Add a link from the item detail page
items.description: When the user submits the link form on an item page, overseer shall create the chosen relation between that item and the entered item ID in the chosen direction.
acceptance_criteria: Given US-0001, when the user picks '→ implements' and enters 'req-0001', then POST /api/links {src:'US-0001', rel:'implements', dst:'REQ-0001'} is sent and the Links list refreshes.
Given '← from' is chosen, when submitted, then the entered item becomes the source and the current item the destination.
Given an invalid relation, when submitted, then the error is shown under the form.

items.title: doctor warns when the embedding model is not downloaded
items.description: If the embedding model files are missing from the local model cache, then overseer doctor shall report the model check as WARN suggesting overseer models pull.
acceptance_criteria: Given an empty model cache, when "doctor --json" runs, then the model check status is WARN with "Xenova/multilingual-e5-small not downloaded (run overseer models pull)"
Given every model file is cached, when overseer doctor runs, then the model check is OK with "<model> cached in <dir>"

items.title: Remove a link from the item detail page
items.description: When the user presses the remove button of a listed link on an item page, overseer shall delete that relation.
acceptance_criteria: Given BUG-0001 affects REQ-0001, when × is pressed on that link, then DELETE /api/links {src:'BUG-0001', rel:'affects', dst:'REQ-0001'} returns {linked:false} and the list refreshes.
Given the removal fails, when the error returns, then an error toast 'Could not remove link: <CODE>: <message>' appears.

items.title: Show the item history timeline on the detail page
items.description: overseer shall show the history events of an item on its detail page in newest-first order.
acceptance_criteria: Given REQ-0001 with events, when #/items/REQ-0001 opens, then GET /api/items/REQ-0001?history=1 is used and each event shows time, actor, channel and a description such as 'status proposed → approved'.
Given an incoming link event recorded on another item, when the timeline renders, then the event is prefixed with the source item ID.
Given a comment event, when the timeline renders, then the comment text is shown as a quote.

items.title: Post comments from the item detail page
items.description: When the user posts a non-empty comment on an item page, overseer shall add it to the history of that item.
acceptance_criteria: Given #/items/US-0001, when the user types 'Started' and presses Comment, then PATCH /api/items/US-0001 {comment:'Started'} is sent, the box clears and the timeline shows 'commented'.
Given a blank comment, when the form renders, then the Comment button is disabled.

items.title: Show coverage counts, drift and traceability on the coverage page
items.description: overseer shall show on the #/coverage page the number of requirements per coverage state, the drift findings and the requirement traceability matrix.
acceptance_criteria: Given requirements in several coverage states, when #/coverage opens, then one count per coverage state from GET /api/reports/summary is shown.

Given drift findings, when the page renders, then a 'Drift (N)' table lists requirement, title, status, coverage, rule, message and work items; with none it reads 'No drift between requirement statuses and work items.'
Given requirements with implementing items and bugs, when the page renders, then the Traceability table lists implemented-by items with their children and affecting bugs with severity.

items.title: Create any item kind from the New item dialog
items.description: When the user submits the New item dialog, overseer shall create an item of the selected kind with the entered fields and links.
acceptance_criteria: Given the New item button on #/requirements or #/coverage, when pressed, then the dialog opens with kind requirement (story on other pages) and offers every kind with kind-specific fields.
Given an empty title or a requirement without type, when Create is pressed, then the dialog shows the problem and sends nothing; empty fields are omitted so server defaults apply.
Given a successful create, when the response arrives, then a toast 'Created <ID>' lists any lint warnings and the browser opens #/items/<ID>; Escape or Cancel closes the dialog.

items.title: Hint similar existing items while typing a new item
items.description: While the user types the title or description of a new item, overseer shall list existing items similar to that text after a 400 ms pause in typing.
acceptance_criteria: Given at least 3 characters of title and description, when typing stops for 400 ms, then POST /api/similar {text, kind} runs and non-weak matches are listed under 'Similar existing items' with similarity percent and match badge.
Given semantic search is unavailable, when hints are shown, then the heading adds '(keyword match)'.

items.title: Confirm before creating a possible duplicate from the board
items.description: If creating an item from the New item dialog returns possible_duplicate, then overseer shall show the candidates with a 'Create anyway' action that resubmits the item with allow_duplicate.
acceptance_criteria: Given a title matching REQ-0001, when Create is pressed, then nothing is created and the notice 'Possible duplicate: nothing was created.' lists the candidates.
Given the duplicate notice, when 'Create anyway' is pressed, then POST /api/items is sent with allow_duplicate:true.
Given the duplicate notice, when the user edits a field or changes the kind, then the notice is cleared.

items.title: Export reports from the board header
items.description: When the user presses the Export button in the board header, overseer shall write the reports into the export folder and list the written files in a notification.
acceptance_criteria: Given export_dir docs/overseer, when Export is pressed, then POST /api/export runs and a toast 'Exported N file(s) to docs/overseer' lists each written path.
Given the export fails, when the error returns, then an error toast 'Export failed: <CODE>: <message>' appears; error toasts stay 10 s, others 7 s.

items.title: Identify the project in the board header and tab title
items.description: overseer shall show the project name in the board header and in the browser tab title.
acceptance_criteria: Given project_name 'shop', when the board loads, then the header shows 'overseer shop' with the root path as tooltip and the tab title is 'shop · overseer'.
Given the board loads, when GET /api/project answers, then it includes the package version and the enum lists (kinds, statuses, priorities, relations, coverage states) the forms use.

items.title: Import skill fetches GitHub/GitLab issues through the harness's own MCP server
items.description: When the user asks to import issues, overseer shall instruct the agent to fetch them through the GitHub or GitLab MCP server configured in the harness.
acceptance_criteria: Given a repository, when the agent follows overseer-import, then it derives host and repo from 'git remote get-url origin' (github.com/owner/repo or <gitlab-host>/group/project).
Given GitHub, when the agent fetches, then it calls list_issues with owner, repo, perPage 100, no state (open and closed) and follows pageInfo.endCursor via after until hasNextPage is false.

Given GitLab, when the agent fetches, then it calls list_work_items with project_id, state all, first 100 and the after cursor, and get_work_item (project_id, work_item_iid) for each item whose body it needs.

items.title: Import skill refreshes incrementally from the last import timestamp
items.description: When a previous import of the same repository exists, overseer shall instruct the agent to fetch only issues updated since that import.
acceptance_criteria: Given report summary lists a last import for github:<owner/repo> or gitlab:<path>, when the agent follows overseer-import, then it passes that time as since (GitHub) or updated_after (GitLab).
Given no previous import or a user request for a full import, when the agent fetches, then it omits the since filter.

items.title: Import skill maps each GitHub/GitLab issue to an ImportItem with a type hint
items.description: When the agent imports issues, overseer shall instruct it to send them to import_items as ImportItems in batches of at most 50.
acceptance_criteria: Given a GitHub issue, when mapped, then external_id is owner/repo#N, issue type Bug/Feature/Task becomes type_hint bug/story/task, and pull requests are skipped.

Given a GitLab work item, when mapped, then external_id is group/project#IID, type Epic/Task/Incident/Requirement becomes epic/task/bug/requirement, type Issue gets no type_hint, and state opened becomes open.
Given 120 mapped issues, when the agent calls import_items({source, repo, items}), then it sends 3 batches of at most 50 items.

items.title: Import skill reports results and proposes links only with user consent
items.description: When an import batch completes, overseer shall instruct the agent to report the created, updated and unchanged counts with item IDs.
acceptance_criteria: Given an import_items result, when the agent reports, then it lists created/updated/unchanged counts with IDs, every warnings entry (e.g. parent not resolved) and each possible_duplicates pair with its similarity.
Given possible duplicates or related items, when the agent proposes duplicates, implements or affects links, then it creates them only after the user agrees.

items.title: Import skill shows per-harness GitHub/GitLab MCP setup when no server is available
items.description: If no GitHub or GitLab MCP tools are available, then overseer shall instruct the agent to show the setup for its harness from references/integrations.md and stop.
acceptance_criteria: Given a harness without GitHub/GitLab MCP tools, when the agent follows overseer-import, then it shows that harness's setup command from references/integrations.md, asks the user to authenticate and stops.
