Given references/integrations.md, when read, then it gives GitHub (read-only issues URL https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/x/issues/readonly) and GitLab (https://<host>/api/v4/mcp with toolsets core,work_items) setup for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Cursor, OMP and OpenCode, marking unverified commands '(unconfirmed)'.
Given no MCP server, when the agent offers an alternative, then it is exporting issues to a JSON array of ImportItems and running overseer import <file> --source github|gitlab --repo <repo>.

items.title: Bootstrap skill discovers requirements from an existing codebase
items.description: When the user asks to bootstrap or reverse-engineer requirements of an existing project, overseer shall instruct the agent to record each behaviour found in its code or docs as a requirement tagged discovered.
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing project, when the agent follows overseer-bootstrap, then it inventories README/docs/ADRs/CHANGELOG, API specs and routes, CLI commands, UI pages, test names, config limits and CI/CD, reading only what is needed.

Given a behaviour present in code, when recorded, then status is implemented with tags ['discovered'], asked_by '(discovered)', source 'discovered: <path>' and code_refs; a documented but absent behaviour gets status proposed with the doc path as source.
Given requirements already exist, when bootstrap runs, then it treats the run as a refresh and updates the matching item (adding code_refs) instead of creating a duplicate.

items.title: Bootstrap skill elicits a new project's requirements with a short interview
items.description: When overseer starts on a new project, overseer shall instruct the agent to elicit initial requirements with a short interview asked one group at a time.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new project, when the agent follows overseer-bootstrap, then it asks about vision, users and roles, the top 3–5 user journeys, constraints, and one NFR prompt per ISO 25010 category, stopping when the user wants.
Given the interview answers, when recorded, then dictated requirements are approved and the agent's suggestions proposed.
Given recorded requirements, when the agent proposes epics (one per journey or area) and INVEST stories with implements links, then it creates them only after the user agrees.

items.title: Codex config.toml MCP server kept inside a delimited overseer-managed block
items.description: When installing for Codex, overseer shall write the `[mcp_servers.overseer]` table inside a block delimited by `# >>> overseer (managed by overseer-cli) >>>` and `# <<< overseer <<<` in config.toml.
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing ~/.codex/config.toml, when install runs, then the block is appended after one blank line with the previous content unchanged; a later install with another node path replaces the single block; uninstall restores the original text.

Given `[mcp_servers.overseer]` already defined outside the block, when install runs, then config.toml is reported skipped with a warning 'already defined outside the overseer managed block', left unchanged, and the codex agent file is still written.

items.title: An error while planning one harness aborts only that harness before any of its writes
items.description: If an error occurs while planning the changes for a harness target, then overseer shall abort only that target before writing any of its files.
acceptance_criteria: Given a malformed ~/.cursor/mcp.json, when install runs for cursor and omp, then one failed action (cursor, CONFIG_PARSE) is reported, the file, cursor agent and shared skills are not written, and ~/.omp/agent/mcp.json is created.

Given a malformed ~/.codex/config.toml, when install runs for codex and gemini, then config.toml is unchanged without a backup, a 'codex: CONFIG_PARSE' warning is reported, and gemini installs including the shared skills.
Given any action with status failed, when `overseer install` or `overseer uninstall` finishes, then the exit code is 1.
items.fit_criterion: A malformed ~/.cursor/mcp.json or ~/.codex/config.toml yields exactly one action with status 'failed' and a message starting 'CONFIG_PARSE: '; the file stays byte-identical with no .overseer-backup and no agent or skill files of that target; the other targets install; `overseer install`/`uninstall` exit with code 1 when any action failed.

items.title: Existing harness config copied to <file>.overseer-backup before overseer changes it
items.description: When overseer is about to change an existing harness config file for the first time in a run, overseer shall copy that file to `<file>.overseer-backup`.
acceptance_criteria: Given ~/.gemini/settings.json exists, when install runs, then settings.json.overseer-backup holds the original text.
Given pre-existing gemini settings.json, codex config.toml and opencode.json, when install then uninstall run in user scope, then .overseer-backup copies of exactly those three files remain.
Given an omp mcp.json created by an earlier install, when install changes its entry, then mcp.json.overseer-backup exists.

items.title: Repeated install with nothing to change reports unchanged and rewrites no file
items.description: When install runs for targets whose files and registrations already match, overseer shall report every action as unchanged without rewriting any file.
acceptance_criteria: Given a completed user-scope install of all seven targets, when install runs again, then every action is 'unchanged', all file mtimes are equal and claude only receives `mcp get overseer`.
Given a completed project-scope install of all seven targets, when install runs again, then every action is 'unchanged' and all file mtimes are equal.

items.title: --dry-run reports planned writes, removals and commands while changing nothing
items.description: While `--dry-run` is set, overseer shall report each install or uninstall write, removal and registration command as planned without changing files or running registration commands.
acceptance_criteria: Given --dry-run with claude and opencode on PATH, when install runs for all targets in user scope, then HOME stays empty, every action is 'planned', and the list includes ~/.codex/config.toml, `claude mcp remove --scope user overseer` and the `claude mcp add …` command.
Given --dry-run, when install runs with claude on PATH, then no claude process is spawned.
Given a project-scope install, when uninstall runs with --dry-run, then every action is 'planned' and the file tree and mtimes are unchanged.

items.title: OpenCode MCP entry and agent follow the config schema of the installed OpenCode major version
items.description: When installing for OpenCode, overseer shall use the v2 config schema if `opencode --version` reports major version 2 or higher, and the v1 schema in every other case.
acceptance_criteria: Given `opencode --version` prints 2.0.3, when installing in project scope, then opencode.json is {mcp: {servers: {overseer: {type: local, command: [overseer, mcp], codemode: false}}}} and the agent frontmatter has mode subagent and permissions [{action: edit, resource: '*', effect: deny}].

Given opencode 1.x or no opencode binary, when installing, then opencode.json has $schema https://opencode.ai/config.json and mcp.overseer {type: local, command: [overseer, mcp], enabled: true}, and the agent has permission.edit deny.
Given either schema, when uninstall runs, then both mcp.overseer and mcp.servers.overseer are removed and an opencode.json left empty is deleted.

items.title: doctor --deep embeds a test string to prove the model loads
items.description: When overseer doctor runs with --deep, overseer shall load the embedding model and report a model load check from embedding a test string.
acceptance_criteria: Given a cached model, when "doctor --deep" runs, then the model load check is OK "embedded a test string (dims 384)"
Given the model cannot be loaded, when "doctor --deep" runs, then the model load check is FAIL with the error message
Given doctor runs without --deep, when the checks are listed, then there is no model load check

items.title: doctor reports the project root, on/off state, schema and item counts
items.description: When overseer doctor runs, overseer shall report a project check with the resolved project root and whether overseer is on for it.
acceptance_criteria: Given an enabled project with one requirement, when "doctor --json" runs, then the project check is OK with "<root> (schema <n>; 1 items: 1 requirement; semantic on|off)"

Given a project that is not turned on, when "doctor --json" runs, then the project check is OK "<root> (overseer is off by default; overseer enable turns it on)" (or "turned off" / "turned off through <folder>" when a rule disables it)

Given the root resolves to the home folder or the filesystem root, when doctor runs, then the project check is WARN "No project detected (resolved to <root>); run inside a project folder or pass --project"

items.title: doctor summarises installed and merely detected harnesses in one line
items.description: When overseer doctor runs, overseer shall report one harnesses line naming the harnesses overseer is installed for at user scope and the detected harnesses that lack it.
acceptance_criteria: Given overseer installed for omp and claude on PATH, when "doctor --json" runs, then the harnesses check is OK "overseer installed for omp; also detected: claude (add with overseer install --targets <ids>)"
Given overseer is installed for no harness, when doctor runs, then the harnesses check is WARN "overseer is not installed for any harness (detected: <ids>); run overseer install"

items.title: doctor inspects agent, skills and MCP entry only for harnesses with overseer
items.description: When overseer doctor runs, overseer shall check the agent file, the skills and the MCP registration only for the harnesses overseer is installed for.
acceptance_criteria: Given overseer installed only for omp and claude on PATH, when "doctor --json" runs, then the omp checks are "omp (user) agent", "omp (user) skills", "omp (user) mcp" and there is no claude check

Given a project root with overseer files for a harness at project scope, when doctor runs there, then that harness also gets "<id> (project) agent/skills/mcp" checks, and harnesses without project files get none
Given claude is installed, when doctor checks its MCP entry, then it runs "claude mcp get overseer" and reports WARN "cannot verify" when claude is not on PATH

items.title: doctor fails a user-scope MCP entry whose node or cli.js path is gone
items.description: If a user-scope MCP registration points to a command or script path that does not exist, then overseer doctor shall report that MCP check as FAIL listing the missing paths.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user-scope MCP entry whose cli.js was moved, when doctor runs, then the MCP check is FAIL "<config file>: missing: <path>"
Given a project-scope MCP entry whose command is not on PATH, when doctor runs, then the MCP check is WARN "'<command>' is not on PATH"
Given the Claude Code registration from "claude mcp get overseer" points to a missing path, when doctor runs, then the MCP check is FAIL

items.title: doctor exits with code 1 when any check is FAIL
items.description: If any overseer doctor check reports FAIL, then overseer doctor shall exit with code 1.
acceptance_criteria: Given "doctor --json", when it runs, then the exit code is 1 exactly when some check in {checks: [{status, label, detail}]} has status FAIL
Given doctor without --json, when it runs, then each check prints as "<STATUS>  <label>: <detail>"

items.title: Subagent file uses each harness's native agent format and frontmatter fields
items.description: When installing for a harness, overseer shall write the overseer subagent in that harness's agent file format with the frontmatter fields that harness reads.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project-scope install, when the Markdown agents are read, then each starts with YAML frontmatter holding name overseer and the shared description, with claude disallowedTools 'Edit, Write, NotebookEdit' and skills [overseer], omp autoloadSkills [overseer], gemini kind local, copilot as .github/agents/overseer.agent.md, cursor model inherit, opencode mode subagent, and each ends with '<!-- managed-by: overseer-cli -->'.

Given the Codex target, when the agent is written, then .codex/agents/overseer.toml starts with '# managed-by: overseer-cli', parses as TOML with name overseer and a developer_instructions literal string.
Given templates/agent-prompt.md containing ''' , when installing for codex, then the codex target fails with INVALID_INPUT and nothing of it is written.

items.title: Shared .agents/skills folder kept while another reader harness still has overseer installed
items.description: When uninstalling a harness that reads the shared `.agents/skills` folder, overseer shall keep the shared overseer skills while another reader harness still has its managed subagent file.
acceptance_criteria: Given codex and gemini installed in user scope, when uninstall runs for codex, then a 'shared' action reports skipped 'still used by gemini' and ~/.agents/skills/overseer/SKILL.md remains; a following `overseer uninstall` targets only gemini and removes ~/.agents/skills/overseer.
Given cursor and opencode installed in user scope, when cursor is uninstalled, then ~/.agents/skills/overseer is removed and ~/.config/opencode/skills/overseer/SKILL.md stays.

items.title: `overseer uninstall` removes managed agent files, skill folders and MCP registrations
items.description: When the user runs `overseer uninstall`, overseer shall remove the managed subagent file, the managed skill folders and the overseer MCP registration of each target harness in the chosen scope.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user-scope install of all targets over pre-existing user files, when `overseer uninstall` runs, then report.targets lists all seven, the Codex TOML block and JSON entries are removed, the last claude call is `mcp remove --scope user overseer`, and only the pre-existing content plus .overseer-backup files remain.
Given gemini is the only harness with a managed subagent file, when `overseer uninstall` runs without --targets, then only gemini is targeted.

Given the claude registration is already absent, when uninstall runs for claude, then the command action is 'unchanged' with message 'not registered' and no warning; without claude on PATH it is a 'manual' step.

items.title: Uninstall deletes config files and folders it leaves empty, up to the home or project root
items.description: When uninstall leaves a config file with nothing but `$schema` or a folder with no entries, overseer shall delete that file or folder, stopping at the home directory or project root.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project-scope install of all seven targets in an empty project, when uninstall runs, then the project folder is empty.
Given a user-scope install and uninstall of all targets, when the folders under HOME are listed, then they equal the list before install.
Given an opencode.json created by install, when uninstall removes the overseer entry, then the file is deleted without a backup.

items.title: User-scope harness paths honour CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME and the other config-dir variables
items.description: While a harness config-dir environment variable is set, overseer shall place that harness's user-scope files under the folder the variable names.
acceptance_criteria: Given CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, CODEX_HOME, COPILOT_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME set, when installing all targets in user scope, then the claude agent and skills, omp mcp.json, codex agents/overseer.toml and config.toml, copilot mcp-config.json and opencode/opencode.json are under those folders and HOME only holds .agents, .gemini and .cursor.
Given PI_CONFIG_DIR=<name> without PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, when installing omp in user scope, then its files go under ~/<name>/agent.

items.title: Per-kind item IDs with a zero-padded sequence
items.description: When an item is created, overseer shall assign it the next ID of its kind in the form <PREFIX>-NNNN, with prefix REQ, EPIC, US, TASK or BUG and a 4-digit zero-padded sequence per kind.
acceptance_criteria: Given an empty registry, when two requirements, an epic, a story, a task and a bug are created, then they get REQ-0001, REQ-0002, EPIC-0001, US-0001, TASK-0001 and BUG-0001

items.title: Lowercase and unpadded ID references resolve to the canonical ID
items.description: When an item ID is given in lowercase, with surrounding spaces or without zero padding, overseer shall resolve it to the canonical ID of that item.
acceptance_criteria: Given REQ-0001 exists, when req-1 is requested, then the item REQ-0001 is returned

items.title: Defaults for fields omitted at item creation
items.description: When an item is created without status, priority, in_backlog or asked_by, overseer shall fill them with the first status of its kind, priority should, in_backlog false and the project default_asked_by.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requirement created with only kind, title, description and req_type, when it is stored, then status is proposed, priority should, in_backlog false, asked_by the git user name, source null and acceptance_criteria and tags empty
Given an epic or a story created without status, when it is stored, then its status is open or backlog respectively

items.title: Statuses limited to the status set of the item kind
items.description: If a create, update or list filter names a status outside the status set of the item kind, then overseer shall reject it with INVALID_STATUS listing the valid statuses.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new requirement, when it is created with status done, then INVALID_STATUS is raised and the message lists proposed, approved, implemented
Given a story, when it is updated to status approved, then INVALID_STATUS is raised
Given any items, when they are listed with status nope, then INVALID_STATUS is raised

items.title: Free transitions between statuses of the same kind
items.description: overseer shall accept a change from any status of an item kind to any other status of the same kind.
acceptance_criteria: Given a story, when its status is set in turn to done, backlog, review, cancelled and ready, then every update succeeds with that status

items.title: delivered_at stamped when an item enters a delivered status
items.description: When an item without delivered_at enters a delivered status (implemented or verified for requirements, done for the other kinds), overseer shall set delivered_at to the current time.
acceptance_criteria: Given a proposed requirement, when it moves to implemented, then delivered_at is set
Given an implemented requirement, when it moves to verified, then delivered_at keeps its earlier value
Given a story created with status done, when it is stored, then delivered_at is set

items.title: delivered_at cleared when an item leaves the delivered statuses
items.description: When an item moves from a delivered status to a status that is not delivered, overseer shall clear its delivered_at.
acceptance_criteria: Given a verified requirement, when it moves to approved, then delivered_at is null
Given a done story, when it moves to cancelled, then delivered_at is null

items.title: status_changed_at updated on every status change
items.description: When an item status changes, overseer shall set status_changed_at to the time of the change.
acceptance_criteria: Given a proposed requirement, when its status is set to approved, then status_changed_at equals the update time
Given an update that leaves the status unchanged, when it is applied, then status_changed_at keeps its value

items.title: One history event per changed field with old and new value
items.description: When an update changes item fields, overseer shall append one history event per changed field holding its old and new value.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requirement, when title, priority, rationale and status change in one update, then update events for title, priority and rationale and one status event are appended with old and new values
Given an update whose values equal the stored ones, when it is applied, then no event is recorded
Given a rationale, when it is cleared with null, then the last event has old_value Compliance and new_value null

items.title: History events for creation, import, links and comments
items.description: When an item is created, imported, linked, unlinked or commented on, overseer shall append a history event with the matching action.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requirement created with title Audited, when its history is read, then the first event is create with new_value Audited
Given an update with comment Agreed in standup, when it is applied, then a comment event holds that text
Given a story, when it is linked to and then unlinked from a requirement, then its history holds a link event and an unlink event naming the requirement

items.title: History event actor from OVERSEER_ACTOR or default_asked_by
items.description: overseer shall record on every history event an actor taken from OVERSEER_ACTOR, falling back to the project default_asked_by.
acceptance_criteria: Given the actor tester in the calling context, when an item is created and updated, then every event has actor tester
Given OVERSEER_ACTOR is unset, when an item changes, then the event actor is the project default_asked_by

items.title: Item detail with outgoing links, incoming links, children and history
items.description: When an item is requested, overseer shall return it together with its outgoing links, incoming links and child items.
acceptance_criteria: Given a story implementing a requirement, when the requirement is requested, then the story is among its incoming links
Given an epic with a child story, when the epic is requested, then the story is listed among its children

Given a request with history, when a requirement linked and unlinked by a story is requested, then its events and the link and unlink events pointing at it come back in sequence order: create, link, update, unlink

items.title: Items are never deleted, only closed through a status
items.description: overseer shall keep every recorded item permanently, closing it only through a status change.
acceptance_criteria: Given an item, when any service, CLI or MCP operation runs, then the item row still exists afterwards
items.fit_criterion: No code path deletes rows from items: the only DELETE statements target links, items_fts, item_embeddings and the vector tables; closing statuses are rejected, obsolete and cancelled.

items.title: Closed items hidden from lists unless requested
items.description: While an item has a closed status (rejected or obsolete for requirements, cancelled for the other kinds), overseer shall omit it from item lists unless closed items or explicit statuses are requested.
acceptance_criteria: Given a proposed and a rejected requirement, when requirements are listed, then only the proposed one is returned
Given the same items, when they are listed with include_closed, then the total is 2
Given the same items, when they are listed with status rejected, then the rejected requirement is returned

items.title: Item listing filtered by kind, status, type, tag and parent, paged by ID
items.description: When items are listed, overseer shall return the items matching the given kind, status, requirement type, tag and parent filters in ID order, paged by limit and offset.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requirement tagged Auth, when items are listed with tag auth, then that requirement is returned
Given a story under an epic, when items are listed with that parent_id, then only the story is returned
Given three open items, when they are listed with limit 2 and offset 1, then total is 3 and the second and third items by ID are returned

items.title: Parent kind rules for the item hierarchy
items.description: If a parent is set that its kind does not allow (story under epic, task under story, bug under epic or story, requirement under requirement, epic without parent), then overseer shall reject it with INVALID_PARENT.
acceptance_criteria: Given an epic, when a task is created with that epic as parent, then INVALID_PARENT is raised
Given an epic, when another epic is created with it as parent, then INVALID_PARENT is raised
Given an epic and a story, when a bug is created under each, then both bugs are stored with that parent

items.title: Parent assignments that create a cycle are rejected
items.description: If setting a parent would make an item its own ancestor, then overseer shall reject the change with INVALID_PARENT.
acceptance_criteria: Given requirement B whose parent is requirement A, when the parent of A is set to B, then INVALID_PARENT is raised

items.title: Relation kind rules and self-link ban for links
items.description: If a link breaks its relation kind rule (implements story/task to requirement, affects bug to requirement/story, refines/conflicts_with/supersedes requirement to requirement, duplicates same kind, depends_on/relates_to any) or points at its own source, then overseer shall reject it with INVALID_LINK.
acceptance_criteria: Given an epic and a requirement, when the epic is linked with implements to the requirement, then INVALID_LINK is raised
Given a story and a task, when the story is linked with duplicates to the task, then INVALID_LINK is raised
Given a requirement, when it is linked with relates_to to itself, then INVALID_LINK is raised

items.title: An implements link puts the target requirement in the backlog
items.description: When an implements link targets a requirement that is not in the backlog, overseer shall set its in_backlog flag to true.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requirement, when a story is created with an implements link to it, then the requirement in_backlog is true
Given that link, when the requirement history is read, then one update event changes in_backlog from false to true
Given the implements link is then removed, when the requirement is read, then in_backlog stays true

items.title: Re-adding an existing link keeps a single link without a new event
items.description: When a link that already exists is added again, overseer shall keep the existing link without recording another event.
acceptance_criteria: Given a story linked with implements to a requirement, when the same link is added again, then the story history holds a single link event
Given no such link, when its removal is requested, then no unlink event is recorded

items.title: Invalid create requests write nothing
items.description: If any field, parent or link of a create request is invalid, then overseer shall reject the request without writing any item, link, event or ID.
acceptance_criteria: Given a story create with one existing and one missing implements target, when it is submitted, then NOT_FOUND is raised and no link exists
Given a story create with an affects link, when it is submitted, then INVALID_LINK is raised and item counts are unchanged
Given those rejected creates, when a valid story is created, then it gets US-0001
items.fit_criterion: After a rejected create, item counts, links and the in_backlog flags are unchanged and the next valid create still gets the first free ID (US-0001).

items.title: Every write runs in a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction with rollback
items.description: overseer shall run every database write inside a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction that is rolled back when the write fails.
acceptance_criteria: Given two service instances on one database, when they create requirements alternately, then they get REQ-0001, REQ-0002 and REQ-0003
items.fit_criterion: Writes go through tx() (BEGIN IMMEDIATE … COMMIT, ROLLBACK on throw, nested calls join the outer transaction); IDs are allocated inside it, so two connections on one database get REQ-0001, REQ-0002, REQ-0003 in turn.

items.title: Shared database access through WAL and a 5000 ms busy timeout
items.description: overseer shall open the project database in WAL mode with a 5000 ms busy timeout so that several processes can use it at once.
acceptance_criteria: Given an opened project database, when PRAGMA journal_mode and busy_timeout are read, then they return wal and 5000
items.fit_criterion: openDatabase runs PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; busy_timeout=5000; foreign_keys=ON; read-only connections set busy_timeout=5000.

items.title: References to missing items rejected with NOT_FOUND
items.description: If a request references an item ID that does not exist, then overseer shall reject it with NOT_FOUND.
acceptance_criteria: Given no EPIC-0099, when a story is created with parent EPIC-0099, then NOT_FOUND is raised
Given no REQ-0042, when a story is linked to REQ-0042, then NOT_FOUND is raised

items.title: Strict item input: unknown fields, kind changes and out-of-range values
items.description: If a create or update request carries an unknown field, a kind change or a value outside its limits, then overseer shall reject it with INVALID_INPUT listing every issue.
acceptance_criteria: Given a story create with field bogus, when it is submitted, then INVALID_INPUT is raised
Given a requirement, when an update sets kind story, then INVALID_INPUT is raised

Given a title empty after trimming or over 500 characters, description or rationale over 20000, other text over 2000, lists over 200 entries, more than 50 links or a negative estimate, when submitted, then INVALID_INPUT is raised

items.title: Kind-specific fields rejected on other kinds
items.description: If a field reserved for some kinds (req_type, nfr_category, fit_criterion, verification_method for requirements; severity, bug_details for bugs; estimate for stories, tasks, bugs) is set on another kind, then overseer shall reject it with INVALID_INPUT.
acceptance_criteria: Given a story create with req_type functional, when it is submitted, then INVALID_INPUT is raised
Given a task create with severity major, when it is submitted, then INVALID_INPUT is raised
Given a requirement create with estimate 3, when it is submitted, then INVALID_INPUT is raised

items.title: Requirement type mandatory when creating a requirement
items.description: If a requirement is created without req_type, then overseer shall reject it with INVALID_INPUT.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requirement create with only a title, when it is submitted, then INVALID_INPUT is raised

items.title: Numbered schema migrations tracked in meta.schema_version
items.description: When overseer opens a project database whose schema_version is below the current version, overseer shall apply each pending numbered migration in its own IMMEDIATE transaction.
acceptance_criteria: Given a database at schema_version 0, when it is opened, then migration 1 runs and meta.schema_version becomes 1
Given a database already at the current version, when it is opened, then no migration runs
items.fit_criterion: MIGRATIONS array in src/core/migrations.ts; SCHEMA_VERSION = its length (1); meta.schema_version advances by one per migration and is re-read under the write lock so a concurrent process never applies a migration twice.

items.title: Timestamps stored as ISO-8601 local time with UTC offset
items.description: overseer shall store every timestamp as ISO-8601 local time with second precision and a UTC offset.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new requirement, when it is stored, then created_at matches YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS±HH:MM

items.title: Project settings read and changed with config get and config set
items.description: overseer shall let users read and change the project settings project_name, default_asked_by, export_dir and board_port with config get and config set.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project, when config set board_port 5000 runs, then config get board_port prints 5000
Given a project, when config get --json runs, then project_name, default_asked_by, export_dir and board_port are returned

items.title: Default project settings when the database is created
items.description: When a project database is created, overseer shall set project_name to the folder name, default_asked_by to git user.name or else the OS user, export_dir to docs/overseer and board_port to 4477.
acceptance_criteria: Given a git repository whose user.name is Test User, when its first requirement is created, then asked_by is Test User
Given a new project database, when config get runs, then export_dir is docs/overseer and board_port is 4477

items.title: Validation of config set keys and values
items.description: If config set names an unknown key, an empty value, a board_port outside 1–65535 or an export_dir outside the project root, then overseer shall reject it with INVALID_INPUT.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project, when config set nope x runs, then it exits with code 1 and INVALID_INPUT
Given a project, when config set board_port 70000 runs, then INVALID_INPUT is raised
Given a project, when config set export_dir ../out runs, then INVALID_INPUT is raised

items.title: User errors carry a code from a fixed set
items.description: If an operation fails because of user input or project state, then overseer shall raise an error carrying one of the codes NO_PROJECT, NOT_FOUND, INVALID_INPUT, INVALID_STATUS, INVALID_LINK, INVALID_PARENT, NOT_MANAGED, CONFIG_PARSE or DISABLED.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requirement create with status done, when it is submitted, then the error code is INVALID_STATUS
Given a missing parent, when an item is created under it, then the error code is NOT_FOUND

items.title: Embeds item texts locally with the multilingual-e5-small model
items.description: overseer shall compute text embeddings on the local machine with the Xenova/multilingual-e5-small q8 ONNX model through transformers.js, using mean pooling with normalised output vectors.
acceptance_criteria: Given the default embedder, when overseer embeds a list of texts, then it runs the Xenova/multilingual-e5-small feature-extraction pipeline with dtype q8, mean pooling and normalize true, and returns one 384-dimension vector per text.
Given any stored item text or search query, when it is embedded with the default model, then the text is prefixed with "query: ".

items.title: Defers loading transformers.js and the model until the first embedding
items.description: overseer shall defer importing transformers.js and loading the embedding model until the first text needs embedding.
acceptance_criteria: Given a CLI command that performs no semantic operation, when it runs, then @huggingface/transformers is never imported.
Given a loaded model, when further texts are embedded in the same process, then the cached pipeline is reused without reloading the model.
items.fit_criterion: TransformersEmbedder.load() runs `await import('@huggingface/transformers')` only on the first embed() or warmup() call; commands that embed nothing never load the onnxruntime native binding.

items.title: Keeps model files in OVERSEER_MODEL_DIR or the per-OS user cache folder
items.description: overseer shall store the downloaded embedding model in the folder named by OVERSEER_MODEL_DIR, falling back to the per-OS user cache folder when that variable is unset.
acceptance_criteria: Given OVERSEER_MODEL_DIR is set, when the model cache folder is resolved, then that folder is used verbatim.
Given OVERSEER_MODEL_DIR is unset on Linux, when the model cache folder is resolved, then it is ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/overseer/models.
Given OVERSEER_MODEL_DIR is unset, when the folder is resolved on macOS or Windows, then it is ~/Library/Caches/overseer/models or %LOCALAPPDATA%\overseer\models respectively.

items.title: `overseer models pull` fetches the embedding model into the cache
items.description: When the user runs `overseer models pull`, overseer shall download the embedding model into the model cache if it is missing, loading it once to confirm it works.
acceptance_criteria: Given a reachable model hub, when `overseer models pull` runs, then it prints `Model Xenova/multilingual-e5-small ready in <cache folder>` and exits with code 0.
Given the download or load fails, when `overseer models pull` runs, then it writes `error: model download failed: <cause>` to stderr and exits with code 1.
Given a model load failed earlier in the same process, when `models pull` runs, then it retries immediately instead of waiting for the retry window.

items.title: Embeds new or changed items before each semantic operation
items.description: When a search, similarity check or coverage check starts, overseer shall embed every item whose vectors are missing or were computed from other text or another model.
acceptance_criteria: Given two embedded items, when one gets a new description and the other only a new status before a search, then only the changed item's text is embedded again.

Given a project embedded with model A, when it is opened with model B and searched, then both vector tables are rebuilt, every item is re-embedded and meta embed_model plus item_embeddings record model B.

Given items to embed, when they are embedded, then each gets a full-text vector (title, description, acceptance criteria, fit criterion; at most 2000 characters) plus a title-only vector, processed in batches of 32 items.

items.title: `overseer reindex` rebuilds every keyword index row and every vector
items.description: When the user runs `overseer reindex`, overseer shall rebuild every item's keyword index row and vectors from the stored item fields.
acceptance_criteria: Given the keyword index rows were deleted, when reindex runs, then it returns {items: 1, semantic: true}, re-embeds the item's full text and title, and a keyword search finds the item again at fts_rank 1.
Given semantic search is unavailable, when reindex runs, then the keyword index is still rebuilt and the result carries semantic false with the warning.
Given the CLI, when `overseer reindex` finishes, then it prints `Reindexed <n> items (semantic: yes|no).` followed by any warning.

items.title: Hybrid search merges keyword and vector rankings by reciprocal rank fusion
items.description: When a search query is given, overseer shall rank items by the sum of 1/(60+rank) over the FTS5 bm25 top 50 and the vector nearest-neighbour top 50.
acceptance_criteria: Given four requirements, when searching 'password reset email', then REQ-0001 ranks first, each hit's score equals the sum of 1/(60+fts_rank) and 1/(60+vector rank), and scores are in descending order.
Given an item that shares no keyword with the query, when searching, then it can still appear through its vector rank with fts_rank null.

Given a kind filter or limit, when searching, then only items of that kind are returned, up to the limit (default 10), each with score, similarity and fts_rank; bm25 weighs title matches twice as much as body matches.

items.title: Keyword index row rewritten on item creation and on text-field changes
items.description: When an item is created or one of its text fields changes, overseer shall rewrite that item's keyword index row in the same transaction.
acceptance_criteria: Given a newly created item, when a keyword search for a word of its title runs, then the item is returned.

Given an update to title, description, rationale, acceptance_criteria, fit_criterion, tags or component, when it commits, then the FTS row holds the title plus a body of description, rationale, acceptance criteria, fit criterion, tags and component.

items.title: Keyword matching ignores accents in both queries and item text
items.description: overseer shall match keyword queries against item text regardless of diacritics on either side.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requirement titled 'Contraseña olvidada', when searching 'contrasena' without semantics, then it is returned.
Given a requirement titled 'Resume upload', when searching 'résumé' without semantics, then it is returned.

items.title: Query text reduced to quoted word tokens before the FTS5 match
items.description: overseer shall turn keyword query text into OR-joined, double-quoted word tokens of at least two letters or digits before running the FTS5 match.
acceptance_criteria: Given the text 'He said "reset" — a ñandú, OK?', when the keyword query is built, then it is '"He" OR "said" OR "reset" OR "ñandú" OR "OK"'.
Given text without any searchable token (such as '?! "'), when searching, then the keyword step is skipped and an empty result is returned without error.

items.title: Similarity check classes the nearest items as duplicate, related or weak
items.description: When asked for items similar to a text, overseer shall return the nearest items by cosine similarity, each classed duplicate at 0.90 or more, related at 0.84 or more, else weak.
acceptance_criteria: Given a stored requirement, when its own title and description are checked, then the verdict is duplicate and the first match is that requirement with match duplicate.
Given no item shares meaning with the text (such as 'Dark theme colors'), when checked, then the verdict is new.

Given any check, when results are returned, then at most limit matches (default 5, optional kind filter) are ordered by similarity = max(full-text, title) cosine similarity and the verdict follows the best match: duplicate, related or new.

items.title: Coverage check answers covered, partially or not_found from the best requirement match
items.description: When asked whether a text is already covered, overseer shall compare it with requirements only, answering covered for a duplicate-class best match, partially for a related-class one, else not_found.
acceptance_criteria: Given a requirement implemented by an in-progress story, when checking 'password reset by email single-use link', then the verdict is partially and the requirement is listed with coverage in_progress and implemented_by US-0001.
Given the same requirement, when checking its exact title and description, then the verdict is covered.
Given no similar requirement, when checking 'Kubernetes autoscaling', then the verdict is not_found.

items.title: Item creation refused while a same-kind duplicate-class match exists
items.description: If a new item's title and description match an existing item of the same kind at duplicate level, then overseer shall return the candidates without writing the item unless allow_duplicate is set.
acceptance_criteria: Given REQ-0001 exists, when the same requirement is created again, then the result is {created: false, reason: 'possible_duplicate', candidates: [REQ-0001 with match duplicate]} and the item count stays 1.
Given allow_duplicate true (CLI `--allow-duplicate`), when the same requirement is created, then it is created and the result lists REQ-0001 under similar.
Given a created item, when the result is returned, then similar lists the duplicate-class and related-class matches found by the check.

items.title: Cross-language matching between English and Spanish item texts
items.description: When a query and an item are written in different languages, overseer shall rate a translation of the item as related or duplicate.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Spanish requirement 'Restablecer la contraseña por correo', when an English password-reset query is checked, then it is the first match with match duplicate or related.

Given an English password-reset requirement, when the Spanish query 'Restablecer la contraseña mediante un enlace enviado por correo' is checked, then it is the first match with match duplicate or related.
Given that requirement, when checking coverage of the short query 'password reset', then the verdict is covered, and 'dark mode theme toggle' gives not_found.

items.title: Classifies at least 80% of the labelled similarity pairs correctly
items.description: overseer shall classify at least 80% of the labelled similarity fixture samples into their labelled class with the default model.
acceptance_criteria: Given the 71 fixture pairs scored in both directions as max(full-text, title) similarity, when classified with duplicate 0.90 and related 0.84, then accuracy is at least 0.8.
Given `npm run calibrate`, when it runs, then it prints per-class n, mean, min and max with suggested thresholds, and the suggested duplicate threshold exceeds the related one.
items.fit_criterion: With OVERSEER_REAL_MODEL=1, at least 0.8 of the 142 directional samples from the 71 pairs in test/fixtures/similarity-pairs.json (25 duplicate, 24 related, 22 unrelated) classify as duplicate (≥ 0.90), related (≥ 0.84) or weak per their label.

items.title: Keyword-only fallback when sqlite-vec or the embedding model is unavailable
items.description: If sqlite-vec fails to load or the embedding model fails, then overseer shall answer searches, similarity checks and coverage checks from the keyword index, flagged semantic false with a warning.
acceptance_criteria: Given no embedder, when searching 'audit', then the result is semantic false with a warning and REQ-0001 at similarity null, fts_rank 1.
Given no embedder, when running a similarity or coverage check, then the verdict is unknown and the keyword matches are listed with similarity null.
Given a model that throws on embed, when the same requirement is created twice, then both creates succeed, the second lists REQ-0001 under similar, and search returns semantic false.
items.fit_criterion: Results carry semantic: false and a warning string; find_similar returns verdict 'unknown' with similarity and match null; check_coverage returns verdict 'unknown'; creates are never blocked; each degradation message is written once per process to stderr as `overseer: <message>`.

items.title: Waits five minutes before retrying a failed embedding model load
items.description: If loading the embedding model fails, then overseer shall reject further load attempts in that process for 5 minutes before trying again.
acceptance_criteria: Given a model load failed less than 5 minutes ago, when another text is embedded, then the call fails at once with 'model load failed recently; retrying later' and semantic operations fall back to keyword results.
Given 5 minutes have passed since the failure, when a text is embedded, then overseer tries to load the model again.
items.fit_criterion: RETRY_AFTER_MS = 300000 in src/core/embeddings.ts; embed() calls within the window fail with 'model load failed recently; retrying later'; warmup() (`overseer models pull`) clears the window.

items.title: Keyword-only search until the embedding model is downloaded
items.description: While the embedding model is not in the model cache, overseer shall answer searches, similarity checks and coverage checks from the keyword index without downloading the model.
acceptance_criteria: Given an empty model cache, when find_similar, check_coverage or search runs, then no download starts and the result has semantic false with a warning that names overseer models pull.
Given an empty model cache, when overseer models pull runs or overseer install runs without --skip-model, then the model is downloaded into the cache.
Given the model is in the cache, when a semantic operation runs, then it uses the model and returns semantic true.

items.title: Installable from the npm registry as overseer-cli
items.description: overseer shall be published on the public npm registry as the package overseer-cli, so that npm install -g overseer-cli installs the overseer command.
acceptance_criteria: Given a machine with Node.js 22.13 or later and no checkout, when npm install -g overseer-cli runs, then overseer --version prints the published version.
Given the globally installed package, when overseer install and overseer board run, then the skill templates and the web board load from the installed package folder.
items.fit_criterion: On a machine with Node.js 22.13 or later and no checkout, npm install -g overseer-cli followed by overseer --version prints the published version.

items.title: Board cards show their priority with a coloured accent and icon
items.description: When the board shows a story, task or bug card, the board shall mark the card's MoSCoW priority with a coloured accent and an icon that differ per priority.
acceptance_criteria: Given cards with each priority, when the board renders, then each card has a left accent and an icon for its priority (must red, should amber, could green, wont grey) and still shows the priority name as text.
Given the light or the dark theme, when the board renders, then every accent has at least 3:1 contrast against the card background.
Given the board header, when it renders, then a legend maps each accent and icon to its priority.

items.title: Order board columns and the requirements table by priority
items.description: When the user chooses priority order, the board columns and the requirements table shall list items from the highest to the lowest MoSCoW priority, keeping ID order among items with the same priority.
acceptance_criteria: Given a column with a could, a must and a should card, when priority order is chosen, then the column lists the must, should and could cards in that order.
Given two cards with the same priority, when priority order is chosen, then the card with the lower ID comes first.
Given priority order is chosen, when a card is dropped into another column, then it appears at its priority position there.
Given the requirements page, when the user sorts by the Priority column, then the rows go from must to wont.
Given priority order was chosen, when the page is reloaded, then the board and the table keep that order.

duplicates.description: When detecting harnesses to install into, overseer shall consider Cursor present if cursor-agent or cursor is found on PATH or a ~/.cursor directory exists.

duplicates.title: La skill explica cómo responder si algo está cubierto
duplicates.description: Cuando el usuario pregunta si algo ya está cubierto, registrado o entregado, overseer deberá indicar al agente que llame a check_coverage con la frase del usuario y responda citando los IDs.

duplicates.title: CLI add command creates items with per-field flags
duplicates.description: Running `overseer add <kind> --title <title>` shall create an item of that kind, setting each field from its corresponding flag.

duplicates.title: Filter the item list by kind, status, type, coverage, tag or parent
duplicates.description: When `overseer list` is given --kind, --status, --type, --coverage, --tag or --parent, it shall print only items matching all of those filters and hide closed items unless --all is passed.

duplicates.title: La instalación falla pidiendo --targets si no hay harness
duplicates.description: Si no se elige ni se detecta ningún harness, overseer install deberá terminar con un error INVALID_INPUT que pida --targets.

duplicates.title: Ignore the .overseer folder via its own .gitignore
duplicates.description: overseer shall make git ignore its data directory by writing a .overseer/.gitignore containing only *, never touching the project's root .gitignore.

duplicates.title: Malformed user config raises CONFIG_PARSE
duplicates.description: If the user configuration file contains invalid JSON or violates the schema, overseer shall stop with a CONFIG_PARSE error that names the file rather than treating it as empty.

duplicates.title: El instalador no toca AGENTS.md ni CLAUDE.md
duplicates.description: overseer deberá limitar lo que escribe la instalación a las carpetas de skills, el archivo del subagente, el archivo de configuración MCP y sus copias de seguridad de cada harness elegido, sin crear ni editar archivos de instrucciones como AGENTS.md o CLAUDE.md.

duplicates.title: Launch the browser at the board when it starts
duplicates.description: When the board server starts and opening the browser is enabled, overseer shall open the default browser at the board URL with `#/board`.

duplicates.title: Done column hides cards completed over 30 days ago
duplicates.description: Unless 'Show all done' is checked, the board shall leave out of the Done column any card whose status last changed more than 30 days ago.

duplicates.title: doctor comprueba sqlite-vec con una tabla vec0 en memoria
duplicates.description: Si sqlite-vec no puede cargarse o crear una tabla vec0 en una base de datos en memoria, overseer doctor deberá marcar la comprobación de sqlite como WARN indicando que solo hay búsqueda por palabras clave.

duplicates.title: Suggest similar items as the user types a new one
duplicates.description: As the user writes the title or description of a new item, the board shall show existing items similar to the text once typing pauses for 400 ms.

duplicates.title: Show MCP setup instructions when GitHub/GitLab tools are missing
duplicates.description: If the agent has no GitHub or GitLab MCP tools, the import skill shall tell it to present the setup steps for its harness from references/integrations.md and then stop.

duplicates.title: La entrada MCP de OpenCode sigue el esquema de su versión mayor
duplicates.description: Al instalar para OpenCode, overseer deberá usar el esquema de configuración v2 cuando `opencode --version` indique la versión mayor 2 o superior, y el esquema v1 en cualquier otro caso.

duplicates.title: Keep shared .agents/skills while another harness still uses them
duplicates.description: When a harness that reads `.agents/skills` is uninstalled, overseer shall leave the shared overseer skills in place as long as another reading harness still has its managed subagent file.

duplicates.title: Any status can move to any other status of its kind
duplicates.description: overseer shall allow an item to change from any of its kind's statuses to any other status of that kind, without a fixed workflow.

duplicates.title: Los ítems nunca se borran, solo se cierran
duplicates.description: overseer deberá conservar para siempre todos los ítems registrados, y solo podrá cerrarlos mediante un cambio de estado.

duplicates.title: A rejected create leaves no trace
duplicates.description: If a create request has any invalid field, parent or link, overseer shall refuse it and write no item, link, event or allocated ID.

duplicates.title: Store timestamps in local ISO-8601 with offset
duplicates.description: overseer shall record all timestamps in ISO-8601 local time, to the second, including the UTC offset.

duplicates.title: `overseer models pull` descarga el modelo de embeddings
duplicates.description: Cuando el usuario ejecuta `overseer models pull`, overseer deberá descargar el modelo de embeddings a la caché si falta y cargarlo una vez para comprobar que funciona.

duplicates.title: check_coverage verdict follows the best requirement match
duplicates.description: When checking whether a text is already covered, overseer shall match it against requirements only and answer covered for a duplicate-level best match, partially for a related-level one and not_found otherwise.

duplicates.title: Priority shown on board cards with colour and icon
duplicates.description: The board shall show each story, task or bug card's MoSCoW priority as a coloured accent plus an icon, distinct for each priority.
